# Ashlr MD

> Ashlr MD is an open-source Markdown desktop app for macOS, Windows, and Linux, with editing, export, local AI, and a bundled MCP server.

Version: 0.4.0. License: MIT. The desktop app is free; optional cloud AI providers may charge fees.

## Source: README.md

Canonical documentation: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/README.md

# Ashlr MD

### Markdown, finally beautiful.

**An open-source, AI-native Markdown app for macOS, Windows, and Linux.** Double-click any `.md` and
it's instantly beautiful: read it, edit it, export it, and understand it with
free, private, **on-device AI** built in.

*Think Preview.app, but Markdown-aware, editable, and AI-native, and cross-platform.*

[![CI](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/actions/workflows/ci.yml)

## 30-second start

1. Download v0.4.0 for your OS from [Releases](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/latest): `.dmg` (Apple Silicon), `.msi`/`-setup.exe` (Windows), `.deb`/`.rpm`/`.AppImage` (Linux).
2. Double-click any `.md` file, or run `mdopen notes.md` after **Preferences → Command-line tool → Install mdopen** (the app's installers leave `mdopen` off your `PATH`; see [docs/AGENTS.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#install)).
3. Ask the AI sidebar about it. On a Mac with Apple Silicon and macOS 26 or later, the built-in on-device model needs no account and no API key: turn on Apple Intelligence in System Settings, then restart Ashlr MD. On Windows and Linux, install [Ollama](https://ollama.com) for free local AI, or add an Anthropic API key in Preferences.

## Connect your agent (MCP)

Easiest: **Preferences → AI agents (MCP) → Connect to Claude Code / Cursor**. By hand, with the bundled `mdopener-mcp`:

```bash
# Claude Code (macOS path shown; Linux: "/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp")
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md "/Applications/Ashlr MD.app/Contents/Resources/mdopener-mcp"
# Codex
codex mcp add ashlr-md -- "/Applications/Ashlr MD.app/Contents/Resources/mdopener-mcp"
```

Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{ "mcpServers": { "ashlr-md": { "command": "/Applications/Ashlr MD.app/Contents/Resources/mdopener-mcp" } } }
```

Windows path: `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ashlr MD\mdopener-mcp.exe`. More in [docs/AGENTS.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md).
The Settings copy command targets a Unix shell on macOS/Linux and PowerShell on
Windows; its quoting is not intended for Windows Command Prompt (`cmd.exe`).


## Why

Your AI agents write Markdown all day: `README.md`, `PLAN.md`, research dumps.
On most systems those open as a wall of raw syntax (TextEdit, Notepad) or a blank
page (Preview). No app owns the simple job of making them *look right* instantly,
especially for non-technical people. Ashlr MD does exactly that, on every platform.

## Features

- **Instant, beautiful rendering**: GFM, Shiki-highlighted code, Mermaid
  diagrams, KaTeX math, GitHub-style callouts, tables, footnotes.
- **Edit without the syntax**: Typora-style WYSIWYG (Milkdown) + a lossless
  source mode (CodeMirror) + a clean Read view. Atomic save; external-change
  detection with a conflict banner.
- **Export anywhere**: one-click **PDF / DOCX / HTML**, fully offline, no Pandoc.
- **⌘K command palette**: fuzzy, keyboard-first access to every action and your
  recent files.
- **Free, private, on-device AI**: summarize / explain / rewrite / translate.
  On **macOS 26+ (Apple Silicon)**: zero-install via **Apple Foundation Models**
  (macOS only). On **Windows & Linux** (and as a fallback on Mac): local
  **Ollama** → your own cloud key → optional hosted. Nothing leaves your device
  unless you opt in.
- **AI superpowers**: select text to Explain / Summarize / Rewrite / Translate;
  **inline AI rewrite in the editor (⌘I)** with Rewrite / Fix grammar / Make
  concise / Expand; **"Explain changes"** when a file changes on disk; and
  chat-with-document.
- **Agent activity drawer (⌘B)**: watch the folder your AI agent writes to and
  new Markdown files appear live; click to open instantly. The answer to "buried
  in agent `.md` files."
- **Outline navigation (⌘⇧O)**: an auto table-of-contents with scrollspy for
  long docs.
- **Tabs**: open several documents at once; the tab bar appears only when more
  than one is open, so the single-file view stays clean. `⌘⇧]` / `⌘⇧[` to switch,
  `⌘W` to close.
- **Find & search**: find-in-document (`⌘F`) in both rendered and source views,
  find-and-replace in source (`⌘⌥F`), and full-text **search across your recent &
  watched files** (`⌘⇧F`).
- **Split view & Zen mode**: edit with a live preview side-by-side (`⌘\`, synced
  scrolling), or go distraction-free with **Zen mode** (`⌘⇧Z`, `Esc` to exit).
- **Obsidian-compatible**: reads your vault natively, with `[[wikilinks]]` (with
  `#heading` / `#^block` anchors and `|aliases`) that resolve vault-wide and open,
  `![[embeds]]` and partial transclusion, sized `![[image.png|300]]` embeds,
  `==highlights==`, hidden `%%comments%%`, and KaTeX math. Read-only **JSON
  Canvas** (`.canvas`) viewing with pan/zoom, plus an **Open in Obsidian** command
  to hand a note back. Never writes to your `.obsidian/` config. Details:
  [**docs/OBSIDIAN.md**](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/OBSIDIAN.md).
- **Reading polish**: word count & reading time, footnote hover previews,
  a path breadcrumb, and copy-link-to-heading on hover.
- **Secure by default**: malicious Markdown is sanitized (no script/HTML
  injection), API keys live in the OS keychain (never plaintext), and a strict
  CSP is enforced. See [SECURITY.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/SECURITY.md).
- **Agent-native review loop**: `mdopen file.md`, the `mdopener://` URL scheme,
  and an **MCP server** so Claude Code / Codex / Cursor can open, read, edit, and
  export the live doc; the **activity drawer (⌘B)** surfaces new agent `.md` files
  the instant they land and **"Explain changes"** narrates each on-disk edit.
  One-click MCP setup in Settings. Full guide: [**docs/AGENTS.md**](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md).
- **Phantom's Markdown viewer**: when Ashlr MD is installed, [Phantom](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom)
  hands its inbox and digest Markdown (`phm inbox show --open`, `phm digest --open`)
  to `mdopen`. The broader "open any `.md`" opener is not on Phantom's `master` yet.
  See [**docs/PHANTOM.md**](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/PHANTOM.md).
- **Obsidian integration**: the [Open in Ashlr MD](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/integrations/obsidian/)
  plugin sends any vault note to Ashlr MD with one click (ribbon, command, and
  right-click) via the `mdopener://` scheme.
- **VS Code integration**: the [Open in Ashlr MD](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/integrations/vscode/)
  extension opens the active `.md` file in Ashlr MD from an editor title-bar
  button (or the command palette) via the `mdopener://` scheme, with a `mdopen`
  CLI fallback.
- **Smart agent output**: callouts, interactive checkboxes that save back to the
  file, and automatic plan / diff / multi-file detection with badges.
- **Three themes**: Paper, Sepia, Midnight (light + dark), switch live.
- **Native & instant**: built on [Tauri 2](https://tauri.app); a tiny native binary
  on every OS, no Electron bloat. MIT, local-first, no telemetry.


## Custom AI endpoints

The AI sidebar, semantic search and the MCP sidecar read these environment variables at call time. Unset or blank means the defaults below, which are what the app always used.

| Variable | Default | Accepts |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | `https://api.anthropic.com` | an `https://` base URL, or `http://127.0.0.1` / `http://[::1]` with optional port; the app appends `/v1/messages` |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | `http://localhost:11434` (MCP sidecar: `http://127.0.0.1:11434`) | `host`, `host:port`, `:port` or a full URL |

**Changed from #131:** `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` must be `https://` (any host), or plain `http://` only for the loopback addresses `127.0.0.1` and `[::1]`. `http://localhost`, plain http to any other host, other schemes, malformed URLs, a user name or password in the URL, a query and a fragment are refused when you send a message: the sidebar shows an error, no request is made and your API key is not sent. Anthropic requests do not follow redirects, so the key goes only to that host. The error never repeats the value.

Trailing slashes are trimmed. This lets a gateway such as a LiteLLM proxy or a Phantom proxy sit in front of Anthropic, or points the app at Ollama on another machine. Only the URL handling is covered by tests; the app has not been tested against a specific gateway. The MCP sidecar accepts an `https://` `OLLAMA_HOST` and applies the same rules as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`: `https://` to any host, or plain `http://` only to `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`. `:port` means `127.0.0.1:port`, and `0.0.0.0` or `[::]` mean the matching loopback address. Any other value (for example `gpu-box:11434` or `http://localhost:11434`) is refused: no request is made and the sidecar falls back to keyword search (a search that asked for `semantic: true` says why in its note). The sidecar does not follow redirects from Ollama. A desktop app launched from the Dock or Start menu may not see variables set in your shell profile.

The installer also reports whether the optional Phantom CLI is installed and which version. It runs only `phantom --version` and never reads or reveals secret values. To run tools with Phantom placeholder keys and base URLs, start them with `phantom exec -- <cmd>`.

### Local models (`localInference`)

**Behavior change for `OLLAMA_HOST`:** the app now accepts `OLLAMA_HOST` only for a loopback host (`127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` or `localhost`; `0.0.0.0` and `[::]` mean the matching loopback address). A remote Ollama such as `gpu-box:11434` is refused (AI and embeddings report an error, no request is made) unless `~/.ashlr/config.json` sets `"localInference": { ..., "allowRemote": true }` AND the URL is `https://`. Only the config file can allow remote, never an environment variable.

To use a local OpenAI-compatible server (Ollama, oMLX, a LiteLLM proxy), add a `localInference` block to `~/.ashlr/config.json`. It uses the same shape as Phantom's (ashlrai/phantom#917):

```json
"localInference": {
  "provider": "ollama",
  "baseUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1",
  "models": { "coder": "qwen3.8:27b" },
  "allowRemote": false
}
```

- `provider` is `ollama` (default base URL `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1`), `omlx` (`http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1`) or `openai-compat` (`baseUrl` required).
- The model defaults to `qwen3.8:27b`. Other options from Phantom's docs/LOCAL-INFERENCE.md: `qwen3.6:27b`, `qwen3.6:35b`, `qwen3-coder:30b` (`ollama pull qwen3.8:27b`). Abliterated or uncensored models are refused.
- The URL must be loopback (`127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` or `localhost`, written exactly). A remote URL needs `allowRemote: true` and `https://`. Refusals use closed codes (`remote-not-allowed`, `remote-requires-https`, `host-not-canonical`, ...) and never repeat the URL.
- No key is ever sent to this endpoint: no Authorization or x-api-key header, not your Anthropic key, not a `phm_` placeholder. If a gateway needs a key, run it through `phantom exec --` so the gateway holds the key itself.
- When the block is valid, the sidebar uses it before any other provider. An invalid block is ignored and never routes anywhere.
- `mdopener-mcp doctor` checks that the server answers: one loopback-only GET of the model list, no key, 3 s timeout, redirects refused, at most 256 KiB read. It prints only a status (`reachable`, `unreachable`, `not-configured`, `config-invalid`, `remote-not-probed` or `bad-response`); `--json` for machines.
- `mdopener-mcp setup --local` gets you from nothing to a working local server. It looks for Ollama on `127.0.0.1:11434` and oMLX on `127.0.0.1:8000` (the same probe as `doctor`: loopback only, no key, 3 s each), probes the `localInference` block when there is one, and prints the exact next steps: the model pull command (`ollama pull qwen3.8:27b`, or the configured model), the `localInference` block to add with `"offline": true`, and the `doctor` check. It downloads nothing and writes nothing: a model is several GB, so you run the pull yourself. Add `--json` for machines (`kind: ashlr.setup-local`, with `downloads: false` and `writes: false`). oMLX has no pull command; it loads models from its dashboard or the folder given to `omlx serve --model-dir`.

### Offline mode

Set `"offline": true` on the same `localInference` block when this machine must not call a cloud model or a model server on another host. The default is off: leaving the key out (or setting `false`) changes nothing.

```json
"localInference": {
  "provider": "ollama",
  "offline": true
}
```

While it is on:

- Chat, embeddings, in-app search and `mdopener-mcp` talk only to loopback: `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]` and `localhost` (that name is pinned to loopback, with no DNS). `127.0.0.2`, `2130706433`, `localhost.evil.com` and a trailing dot are refused. A remote `baseUrl` or `OLLAMA_HOST` is refused even when `allowRemote` is true, and no environment variable can add a host.
- Anthropic and the hosted Ashlr endpoint are not called at all, including through a loopback gateway. The error is `Offline mode (localInference.offline in ~/.ashlr/config.json): cloud AI is disabled. No request was sent.` There is no fallback to another cloud provider.
- A loopback Ollama or `localInference` server still works. On-device Apple Foundation Models are unchanged. Requests still send no API key or OAuth token to a local URL, follow no redirects, and do not use a proxy for loopback.
- A value that is present but not a boolean counts as offline (a typo cannot turn the guarantee off). The `localInference` block itself must still be a boolean or it is invalid and is not used.
- `mdopener-mcp doctor` reports it: a second line, `doctor: offline [ok] verified`, when `offline` is on, the configured server is loopback and it answered the model-list probe, so no remote endpoint is in use and cloud AI is refused. `offline [warn] unverified` means `offline` is on but no loopback server answered (AI is unavailable until one does; `mdopener-mcp setup --local` says what to run). `offline [info] not enabled` means the flag is off. `doctor --json` adds the same as an `offline` check (`native_status` `verified`, `unverified` or `not-enabled`) to the `ashlr.doctor` envelope, after the `local-inference` check; `info` never raises the top-level status.

## Platform support

|---|---|---|---|
| Core (render · edit · export · themes) | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Default `.md` handler | ✅ one-click (Launch Services) | ✅ registers association (opens Settings to confirm) | ✅ via `xdg-mime` |
| Free local AI (zero-install) | ✅ Apple Foundation Models (macOS 26+, Apple Silicon) | Ollama (install separately) | Ollama (install separately) |
| `mdopen` CLI & `mdopener://` deep link | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| MCP server | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |
| Command palette · activity drawer · inline AI · outline | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ |

## One-click agent setup

Open **Preferences → AI agents (MCP)** and click **Connect to Claude Code** or
**Connect to Cursor**; no terminal required. For Codex, copy the command from the
same panel. The **Agent Activity drawer (⌘B)** is the recommended way to watch an
agent's output folder and open new `.md` files the moment they appear. Full guide
+ config snippets: [**docs/AGENTS.md**](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md).

## Download & install

Downloads are on the [GitHub Releases page](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases).
Full, per-OS instructions live in [**docs/INSTALL.md**](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md).

| Platform | Download (latest release) |
|---|---|
| macOS (Apple Silicon only) | `.dmg` (drag to `/Applications`) |
| Windows (x64) | `.msi` or NSIS `-setup.exe` installer |
| Linux (x86_64) | `.deb` · `.rpm` · `.AppImage` |

Auto-update is built in on every platform. Intel Macs aren't covered by the
current release; build from source (below).

> **Note:** Release builds aren't code-signed yet. On macOS the app isn't
> notarized, so right-click the app and choose **Open** the first time. On
> Windows you may see a SmartScreen warning ("More info → Run anyway"). There
> are no Homebrew, winget or AUR packages yet; use the release downloads. See
> [docs/RELEASING.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md).

There's also a one-shot installer that builds from source, installs the `mdopen`
CLI, and wires up Claude Code:

```bash
bash scripts/install.sh
```

The full macOS source installer builds the Swift sidecars declared in the app's
bundle configuration. It needs Xcode 26 / Swift 6.2+ with the macOS 26 SDK for
`mdopener-afm`; a missing sidecar stops packaging with its build instructions.
For the Rust CLI and MCP server only, use `SKIP_APP_BUILD=1 bash scripts/install.sh`;
on Linux that is all the script installs (get the app from the release packages).

## Develop

Prerequisites: [Rust](https://rustup.rs) and [Bun](https://bun.sh).
On macOS, also install Xcode Command Line Tools (`xcode-select --install`).
On Windows, install the [MSVC build tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/).
On Linux, install `build-essential` (Debian/Ubuntu) or equivalent, plus the
[Tauri Linux dependencies](https://tauri.app/start/prerequisites/#linux).

```bash
bun install
bun run tauri dev        # hot-reloading desktop app
bun run tauri dev -- -- file.md   # open a file on launch
```

Quality gates (all green in CI):

```bash
bun run typecheck        # tsc --noEmit
bunx biome check src     # lint + format
bun run test             # Vitest unit tests
cargo check --workspace --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml
```

Source-only MCP setup checks (Python 3, Rust, and Bash; no installer or agent
CLI execution): `python3 scripts/test-mcp-setup.py`.

The on-device AI sidecar (optional, macOS 26+) builds separately:

```bash
cd src-tauri/bins/mdopener-afm && ./build.sh
```

## Architecture

| Layer | What |
|---|---|
| `src/` | React 19 + TS frontend: renderer (remark/rehype + Shiki/Mermaid/KaTeX), Milkdown & CodeMirror editors, AI sidebar, export, Zustand stores |
| `src-tauri/src/` | Rust core: file I/O, watcher, deep links, AI proxy (reqwest), loopback IPC, on-device AI bridge |
| `src-tauri/bins/` | `mdopen` CLI · `mdopener-mcp` MCP server · `mdopener-afm` Swift on-device AI sidecar |
| `landing/` | The marketing site (static, deploy-anywhere) |

See [`docs/VISION.md`](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/VISION.md) for the north star and
[`docs/RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md) for the release process.

## Repair with doctor --fix

`mdopener-mcp doctor --fix` previews repairs to Ashlr MD's state folder, `~/.mdopener`, and writes nothing (exit 0). `mdopener-mcp doctor --fix --apply` makes them. `mdopener-mcp doctor --apply` without `--fix` is refused with exit 2. Add `--json` for one `{ mode, plan, outcome }` object. This is in source (main, 0.4.1 unreleased) and not yet in a release.

```console
$ mdopener-mcp doctor --fix
doctor --fix (dry run, nothing written):
  would fix  make owner-only (0644 to 0600): ~/.mdopener/ipc-port
  would fix  move aside a saved review that does not parse: ~/.mdopener/reviews/<file>.json
Run `mdopener-mcp doctor --fix --apply` to make these changes (a file's contents are backed up before it is moved).
  manual     ipc-token is mode 0644: other users may read the app's token. It is a secret, so doctor --fix never touches it; run: chmod 600 ~/.mdopener/ipc-token
```

What it repairs: owner-only permissions (`~/.mdopener`, `sessions/` and `reviews/` to 0700; session files, saved reviews and `ipc-port` to 0600), reporting the previous mode, and a saved review that is oversized, does not parse, has another schema or sits under another file's name, which is backed up to `<file>.bak-<UTC stamp>` and removed. What stays manual: `ipc-token` permissions (it is the app's secret, so the tool never opens or changes it; run `chmod 600 ~/.mdopener/ipc-token` yourself), symlinks and special files, and MCP client registration (Preferences > AI agents). The `manual` line still prints after `--apply`. Unix only. Details: [docs/doctor-fix.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/doctor-fix.md). To repair every Ashlr tool at once, see [Repair everything](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-stack/blob/main/docs/getting-started-ecosystem.md#repair-everything) in the Ashlr Stack guide.

## Part of the Ashlr ecosystem

Ashlr MD is one of the open-source tools from [Ashlr.AI](https://ashlr.ai). Each
one installs and runs on its own:

- **[Phantom](https://phm.dev)** (`phm`): the agent workbench. Source:
  [ashlrai/phantom](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom).
- **[Phantom Secrets](https://phm.dev/secrets)** (`phantom`): keeps real API keys
  out of agent context with `phm_` placeholders. Source:
  [ashlrai/phantom-secrets](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom-secrets).
- **[Locus](https://github.com/ashlrai/locus)** (`locus`): pins each agent session
  to one account.
- **[Lexicon](https://lexicon.ashlr.ai)** (`lexicon`): fixes the words dictation
  gets wrong.
- **[Ashlr Stack](https://stack.ashlr.ai)** (`stack`): provisions services and
  stores their keys in Phantom Secrets.
- **[ashlr-plugin](https://plugin.ashlr.ai/)** (`ashlr-plugin`): token-efficiency
  tools for Claude Code and Codex.

**Post-quantum readiness:** [docs/PQ-READINESS.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/PQ-READINESS.md) records what Ashlr MD does with cryptography today (no primitives implemented in the application source; dependencies such as `keyring`, `reqwest` and `tauri-plugin-updater` bring their own, not audited there) and what a migration would touch. It makes no claim that Ashlr MD is quantum-safe.

## Source: docs/AGENTS.md

# Using Ashlr MD with AI Coding Agents

Ashlr MD ships an **MCP server** (`mdopener-mcp`) that lets AI coding agents
open, read, edit, search, export, and **request human review of** the document
that is live in your Ashlr MD window, without leaving their coding environment.

It also ships **`mdopen`**, a tiny CLI companion for opening any `.md` file from
a terminal or agent script, and for wiring up an **auto-open hook** that pops
Markdown into Ashlr MD the moment your agent writes it.

> **Tip:** To watch everything an agent produces, open the **Agent Activity
> drawer** (`⌘B` on macOS, `Ctrl+B` on Windows/Linux) and point it at the folder
> your agent writes to. New Markdown files appear live as they're created; click
> any one to open it instantly. It's the recommended way to keep an eye on an
> agent's `.md` output without polling the filesystem yourself.

---

## What the integration is

There are two cooperating pieces:

1. **`mdopener-mcp`**: a [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/)
   server speaking JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio. Agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor,
   anything MCP-capable) launch it as a child process and call its **tools**,
   read its **resources**, and use its **prompts**. It talks to the running
   Ashlr MD app over a token-authenticated loopback HTTP channel (see
   [Security](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#security)).
2. **`mdopen`**: a CLI for opening files (`mdopen file.md`), reading stdin
   (`cat x.md | mdopen -`), and running as a Claude Code **PostToolUse hook**
   (`mdopen --hook`) so freshly written Markdown auto-opens for review.

The MCP server understands the MCP lifecycle (`initialize` →
`notifications/initialized` → `tools/list` / `tools/call`, plus `ping`,
`resources/*`, and `prompts/*`) and negotiates one of three protocol revisions:
**`2024-11-05`**, **`2025-03-26`**, or **`2025-06-18`** (default). It echoes the
client's requested `protocolVersion` when it's one of these, and otherwise
advertises the latest, `2025-06-18`. A JSON-RPC batch (an array of messages,
which `2025-03-26` clients may send) gets one array reply; a message without
an `id` is a notification and gets no reply. A `notifications/*` method
sent *with* an `id` is answered `-32600`, so the client is not left waiting.
A message whose `jsonrpc` is not `"2.0"`, whose `params` is not an object, or
whose `id` is not a string or an integer (MCP never allows `null`) is answered
`-32600` Invalid Request.

The `initialize` result carries `instructions`, which clients may give the
model: the tools to start with (`open_file`, `present_document`,
`request_review`, `get_current_content`, `edit_document`), that only
`open_file` starts the app, what to do when Ashlr MD is not installed (ask the
user to install it from the releases page), and the tools that work without
the app: `export_text` and `export_metadata` (with `path`), `diff_documents`
and `edit_canvas`, `search_vault` (with `vault`), `get_user_annotations` (task
checkboxes only), `list_ai_actions` and the two conversation tools. The text
used to say they all work "on files on disk" and to pass `path` to
`diff_documents`, which takes `path_a` and `path_b`.

---

## Quick start: one-click setup (in-app)

Open **Ashlr MD → Preferences → AI agents (MCP)** and click:

- **Connect to Claude Code**: runs `claude mcp add` for you, no terminal needed.
- **Connect to Cursor**: writes/merges `~/.cursor/mcp.json` automatically.
- **Connect to Codex**: runs `codex mcp add` for you.
- **Auto-open agent Markdown**: installs a Claude Code `PostToolUse` hook so written
  `.md` files open in Ashlr MD automatically (see [Auto-open hook](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#auto-open-hook)).

The **Connect** buttons are only enabled for tools detected on your machine
(`claude` / `codex` on `$PATH`, or a `~/.cursor` directory for Cursor). For a
tool that is not detected, a note under the buttons says how to install it;
detection runs again when you reopen Preferences. For any other agent, copy
the command with the **Copy** button and paste it in a terminal.

When Claude Code or Codex already has an `ashlr-md` server, the Connect button
asks it (`mcp get`) which program it runs. A registration for a program that no
longer exists (the app was moved or reinstalled) is removed and added again for
this app; one that runs another program that still exists is kept, and the
message names it and the command that removes it.

---

## Claude Code

### One-click (recommended)

Open **Preferences → AI agents (MCP)** and click **Connect to Claude Code**.
Ashlr MD runs the following for you (with `<mcp-binary>` resolved to the bundled
`mdopener-mcp` path):

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md <mcp-binary>
```

The `--scope user` flag registers the server globally (all projects), not just
the current directory. Re-running Connect when `ashlr-md` is already registered
is safe: Ashlr MD asks Claude Code (`claude mcp get ashlr-md`) which program it
runs. A registration that already runs this app's server is left alone; one
whose program no longer exists (the app was moved or reinstalled) is removed and
added again with the current path; one that runs another program that still
exists is kept, and the message names that program and the
`claude mcp remove --scope user ashlr-md` command that removes it.

### Manual

```bash
# macOS
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md "/Applications/Ashlr MD.app/Contents/Resources/mdopener-mcp"

# Windows (PowerShell): verify path; shown here for a typical per-user install
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Ashlr MD\mdopener-mcp.exe"

# Linux (.deb install default)
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md "/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp"

# Linux AppImage, without the app: copy the server out once, then register the copy
./AshlrMD.AppImage --appimage-extract "usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp"
install -D "squashfs-root/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp" ~/.local/bin/mdopener-mcp
rm -rf squashfs-root
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md ~/.local/bin/mdopener-mcp
```

An AppImage mounts itself at a new `/tmp/.mount_*` directory on every launch
and unmounts when it quits, so a path inside the mount stops working once the
app closes. From an AppImage, the **Connect** buttons, the **Copy** command and
**Auto-open agent Markdown** therefore copy `mdopener-mcp` (and `mdopen`) to
`~/.local/share/app.mdopener.desktop/bin/` and register that copy, which stays
put after the app quits. The copy is refreshed whenever you click one of them
after updating the AppImage. The AppImage commands above are only needed when
you register the server without opening the app; copy the server out again
after you update the AppImage.

After running it, **restart Claude Code** (quit and start a new session) once.

To get the exact command (with the real binary path) for your machine, use the
**Copy** button in **Preferences → AI agents (MCP)**; it produces precisely:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md <resolved-mdopener-mcp-path>
```

### Verify

```bash
claude mcp list
# macOS:   ashlr-md  /Applications/Ashlr MD.app/Contents/Resources/mdopener-mcp
# Windows: ashlr-md  C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Ashlr MD\mdopener-mcp.exe
# Linux:   ashlr-md  "/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp"
```

### Using the tools in Claude Code

Once the server is registered, Claude Code can call the tools automatically when
you're working on a Markdown file. You can also prompt it explicitly:

```
Open my plan.md in Ashlr MD and show me its current content.
```

```
Edit the open document: change the heading "## Goals" to "## Objectives", then ask me to review it.
```

---

## Codex (OpenAI Codex CLI)

### One-click (recommended)

Open **Preferences → AI agents (MCP)** and click **Connect to Codex**. Ashlr MD
runs the following for you:

```bash
codex mcp add ashlr-md -- <mcp-binary>
```

This writes an `[mcp_servers.ashlr-md]` table to `~/.codex/config.toml`. Codex
consumes MCP **tools** (not resources/prompts), exactly what `ashlr-md` exposes
for agent control.

### Manual: `codex mcp add`

```bash
# macOS
codex mcp add ashlr-md -- "/Applications/Ashlr MD.app/Contents/Resources/mdopener-mcp"

# Windows (adjust to your install dir)
codex mcp add ashlr-md -- "C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Ashlr MD\mdopener-mcp.exe"

# Linux (.deb)
codex mcp add ashlr-md -- "/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp"
```

### Manual: `config.toml`

If you prefer editing config directly, the `codex mcp add` command above writes
the equivalent of this to **`~/.codex/config.toml`** (global) or a project-level
**`.codex/config.toml`**:

```toml
[mcp_servers.ashlr-md]
# macOS:
command = "/Applications/Ashlr MD.app/Contents/Resources/mdopener-mcp"
# Windows (adjust to your install dir):
# command = "C:\\Users\\<you>\\AppData\\Local\\Ashlr MD\\mdopener-mcp.exe"
# Linux (.deb):
# command = "/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp"
args = []
```

Codex picks up the new server on its next invocation (no restart needed).

---

## Cursor

### One-click (recommended)

Open **Preferences → AI agents (MCP)** and click **Connect to Cursor**. Ashlr MD
writes/merges the entry in `~/.cursor/mcp.json` for you, leaving any other
servers untouched. A file it cannot merge (not valid JSON, for example with a
comment or a trailing comma, or whose `mcpServers` is not an object) is left
as it is and the button says why; fix it, or add the entry by hand as below.

### Manual

Edit (or create) **`~/.cursor/mcp.json`** (macOS/Linux) or
`%USERPROFILE%\.cursor\mcp.json` (Windows), the file **Connect to Cursor** writes:

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "ashlr-md": {
      "command": "/Applications/Ashlr MD.app/Contents/Resources/mdopener-mcp",
      "args": []
    }
  }
}
```

On **Windows**, replace `command` with the path to `mdopener-mcp.exe` in your
install directory (e.g. `C:\Users\<you>\AppData\Local\Ashlr MD\mdopener-mcp.exe`).
On **Linux**, use `"/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp"` (`.deb`), or for an
AppImage the copy **Connect to Cursor** makes,
`/home/<you>/.local/share/app.mdopener.desktop/bin/mdopener-mcp`, or the one
made in the manual Claude Code steps above (a path inside the AppImage's
mount changes every launch).

If the file already has other servers, merge only the `"ashlr-md"` key into the
existing `"mcpServers"` object; don't replace the whole file.

After saving, go to **Cursor Settings → MCP** and click **Reload** (or restart
Cursor). You should then see `ashlr-md` listed with a green status indicator.

---

## MCP tool reference

The `mdopener-mcp` server exposes **20** tools over stdio JSON-RPC 2.0.
Every tool returns its payload inside the standard MCP `content` envelope
(`{ "content": [{ "type": "text", "text": "…" }], "isError": false }`); the
"Returns" column below describes the JSON carried inside that text.
Rows are in `tools/list` order: the destructive tools are listed last,
`edit_canvas` (which rewrites a canvas file in place), `export` (which can
replace a file) and the two that replace the whole document,
`replace_document` and `set_content`, so reach for `edit_document` first.

| Tool | Parameters | Returns | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `open_file` | `path: string`, `mode?: "read"\|"edit"` | `{ opened, response }` or `{ opened, method: "url-scheme", confirmed?, note? }` | Opens a file in the Ashlr MD window. `response` is the running app's reply; `method: "url-scheme"` means the app was not reachable and the `mdopener://` URL was handed to the OS launcher, with `confirmed: false` and a `note` when the launcher had not finished within 10 s. **The only tool that launches the app** if it isn't running (falls back to the `mdopener://` URL scheme). Without `mode` the window keeps its current view (a file already open in a tab keeps its own, and an app this call launches starts in `read`); pass `read` before an `export`, which needs Read view. Only Markdown documents that are not dotfiles can be opened (see [Security](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#security)); another file is refused with "Refusing to open `path` '<absolute path>': only Markdown documents (…) that are not dotfiles can be opened." (`present_document` and `request_review` say "present" and "review"). A file that does not exist is refused (by the running app, or before launching it). A running app answers once its window has opened the file, so a file the window could not open (for example, one it cannot read) is a tool error with the reason, also when `path` is the document already open (a failed read of it used to be reported as opened, because that document was still the one open afterwards). A running app that answers with a server error or not in time is a tool error too, never retried through the URL scheme (which could open the file twice). An app that refuses this server's token (HTTP 401) gets the refused-token message (see [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#troubleshooting)) and nothing is launched: the URL scheme would reach the same app. |
| `get_current_content` | none | `{ path, content }` | Path + full Markdown source of the open document. `path` is the absolute path of the document's file: the app opens only files, so it answers `path: null` only when no document is open (its welcome screen, with empty content); this row used to say `null` meant an unsaved document, and the app has none. A `path: null` answer is no document whatever its `content` (it used to be refused only with empty content, here, in `mdopener://current`, the prompts and `export_text` / `export_metadata`, so a buffer with no file read as a document), as the edit tools treat it. With no document open the result is `isError: true` ("No document is open in Ashlr MD. Open one first (open_file)."), as `mdopener://current` (`-32002`) reports it. `export_text` and `export_metadata` without `path` are `isError: true` too, but say to pass `path` instead ("No document is open in Ashlr MD; pass `path` to read a file."). |
| `list_recent` | `limit?: integer` | `[ { path, fileName, openedAt }, … ]` | Recently opened files, most recent first (`openedAt` is milliseconds since the Unix epoch). `limit` defaults to `10`; a value that is not a whole number from 1 to 200 is refused (`-32602`). Needs the app running (it keeps the list): it does not start it, so with the app closed it is an error, and `open_file` starts the app. |
| `request_review` | `path?: string`, `content?: string`, `blocking?: boolean`, `timeout_ms?: integer`, `wait_ms?: integer`, `review_id?: string` | `{ verdict, reviewId, comments }` or `{ status: "pending", reviewId }` | **BLOCKING human sign-off.** See [Human review loop](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#human-review-loop). One of `path`, `content` or `review_id` is required; an empty or whitespace-only `content` is refused with `-32602` (it used to register a review of no text). `verdict` is `approved`, `changes_requested`, `dismissed`, `timeout` or `superseded` (a newer review replaced it in the panel). Needs the app running: it does not start it, so call `open_file` first when the app is closed. |
| `get_user_annotations` | `path: string` | `{ path, verdict, comments, late, tasks, tasksNote?, appRunning?, appAuthFailed?, note? }` | The human's latest review verdict + comments for that file (`verdict` and `comments` are `null` when no review of it was requested), plus its GFM task-checkbox states, read where the page shows a checkbox (`> - [ ] t` and `1. [ ] t` are tasks; a `- [ ]` line in fenced or indented code or front matter is not, and `- [x]` with nothing after it is text): from the live buffer when it is the open document, else from the Markdown file on disk (none for other files). A file on disk larger than 16 MiB (or not UTF-8 text) is not read: `tasks` is empty and `tasksNote` says why, then "Its tasks were not read." (that sentence used to run on from a reason with no full stop). Works without the app: the tasks are read from the file on disk, `verdict` and `comments` come from the review the app saved in `~/.mdopener/reviews/` (null when none; `stale: true` when the file changed since), and `appRunning: false` with a `note` says so. An app that answers HTTP 401 (a stale `~/.mdopener/ipc-token`, or another instance on the port) gets the same disk read, with `appAuthFailed: true` and a `note` naming the token and saying to quit and restart Ashlr MD. Read-only. |
| `edit_document` | `find: string`, `replace: string`, `save?: boolean`, `path?: string` | `{ ok: true, replaced: 1 }` | **Exact, unique find/replace** on the open document. See below. With no document open it returns `isError: true` ("No document is open in Ashlr MD; open one first (open_file).", as `set_content` says) and nothing is applied (it used to say that `find` was not found). A `find` that is not found or not unique, or a `path` that is not the open document, returns `isError: true` with the reason and leaves the document unchanged; a `find` that is not found (here and in `stream_edit` and `stream_edit_apply`) says it must match exactly, whitespace included (a line break matches LF or CRLF), and to copy it from `get_current_content` (it used to stop at "not found"). As for `set_content`, at most two edits wait on the app at once. A window that does not answer within 4 s returns `isError: true` too, but it may still apply the edit, so the error says to call `get_current_content` to see whether it did before retrying (this row used to count it among the refusals that leave the document unchanged). With `save: true`, a save that fails returns `isError: true` saying the edit was applied but not saved; `stream_edit_apply` does the same. The app opens only files (with none it shows its welcome screen), so every document it shows has one: both descriptions used to promise an "applied but not saved" result for "a document with no file yet", and the window applied an edit to a buffer with no file that was not empty, out of sight; it now refuses any state with no file as "No document is open", as `set_content` does. |
| `search_vault` | `query: string`, `limit?: integer`, `semantic?: boolean`, `vault?: string` | `{ results, mode, query?, note?, vault?, truncated?, depthCut? }` | Search across the vault (watched folder) + recents. `query` comes with mode `grep` only: the query as the app's own search read it. The app lists the watched folder's 200 most recently changed Markdown files (the app sends that cap with its vault list, and the `note` quotes the app's number); when the folder has more, the result has `truncated: true` and a `note` saying only those were searched (the Activity drawer says so too). The app keeps the newest files of the whole folder while it walks it, but reads at most 50,000 directory entries and enters folders at most 8 levels down; past the entry budget the walk stops, and below that depth a folder is skipped. Either way the list is the newest of the files it reached, and `truncated: true` comes with a `note` saying newer files elsewhere in the folder may have been missed. When the depth limit is what cut the walk, the result also has `depthCut: true` and the `note` says the folder is too deeply nested (with only the entry budget, there is no `depthCut` and the `note` says the folder is too large); the app's `/vault` reply carries the same `scanCut` (either limit) and `depthCut` (the depth limit) flags. An older app that sends no `depthCut` gets the note naming both limits. Semantic (Ollama `nomic-embed-text` embeddings) when Ollama is reachable on `127.0.0.1:11434`, otherwise case-insensitive grep; `semantic` forces one or the other. `mode` is `semantic`, `grep` (the app's own search), or `grep-local` (the app's search failed, so the vault files were grepped on disk). When semantic search was tried but unavailable (for example `semantic: true` with Ollama down), or the app's search refused or failed, `note` says so in words and quotes the reason. When only some documents fail to embed, the semantic results leave them out and `note` says how many. In every mode, a vault or recent Markdown file that cannot be read (not UTF-8 text, larger than 16 MiB, or a read error) is not searched, and `note` says so (in mode `grep` from the app's `/search` reply, which lists such files as `unread: [{ path, reason }]`, the first 20, with `unreadCount` for all; an app that predates those fields gives no such note): how many files, the first three by path with the reason ("1 file was not searched because it could not be read: /v/latin.md (not UTF-8 text (byte 4 is not valid UTF-8, on line 1)). Convert a file that is not UTF-8 to UTF-8 to make it searchable."), and how many more; such files used to be left out in silence. (Mode `semantic` embeds the files itself; the app's own semantic index, which grounds its "My library" chat, is separate, and Settings > Semantic search names the files a reindex could not read.) if the app refused and the on-disk grep cannot run either, the refusal is the error. `limit` defaults to `50` and is a whole number from 1 to 200 in every mode; a value outside that range is refused with `-32602`, by the tool and by `text://vault-search?…&limit=`, as for `list_recent` (a value above 200 used to be read as 200). Needs the app (it supplies the vault file list). When the app cannot be reached (no `~/.mdopener/ipc-port`, or nothing listening) or refuses this server's token (HTTP 401), but not when it refuses the request, `vault` names a directory (absolute, relative to the server's working directory, or under `~/`) whose Markdown files are searched on disk instead: `mode` is `grep-disk` (or `semantic`), `vault` is the directory searched, and `note` says the app was unreachable and the disk was searched. After a 401 the `note` (here and in mode `grep-local`) gives the cause and the fix of the refused-token message (see [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#troubleshooting)) instead of quoting the raw "IPC auth failed" text. The walk reads only Markdown files that are not dotfiles, skips hidden folders, `node_modules` and `target`, does not follow directory symlinks, and stops at 5000 files (the `note` says so). A file symlink is followed: the file it resolves to is searched, and listed by that resolved path, when it is a Markdown file that is not a dotfile, even if it is outside `vault` (a link's own name is judged too, so a link named `.notes.md` is skipped). It enters folders at most 16 levels below `vault`; a deeper folder is not searched, and the result then has `truncated: true`, `depthCut: true` and a `note` saying so (deeper folders used to be skipped in silence). Without `vault`, an unreachable app or a refused token is `isError: true`, and the message names `vault` (after a 401 it is the refused-token message followed by "To search without the app, pass `vault`: the directory of Markdown files to grep on disk."; it used to be the refused-token message alone). A `vault` that is not a directory, or is itself a hidden folder (`.git`, `.obsidian`), is `isError: true`. |
| `present_document` | `path?: string` | `{ ok, path }` | Open a file (if `path` given) and switch the app into a distraction-free reading presentation (Read view in Zen mode: the title bar, tabs, status bar and side panels are hidden, the window keeps its size, and Escape leaves it; this row and the tool description used to call it full-screen, but the window is not made full-screen), ideal for showing a finished result. Without `path` it presents the open document, and is an error when none is open that names the next step ("No document is open to present. Pass `path` to present_document, or call open_file with the document's `path` first."; the window used to answer only "No document is open to present."). A `path` that does not exist is refused before the app is asked, so the error says so even when the app is not running. It answers once the window has opened and presented the document, and a failure there is a tool error with the reason. Needs the app running: it does not start it, so call `open_file` first when the app is closed. |
| `list_ai_actions` | `include_prompts?: boolean` | `{ actions, count }` | The editor's AI transform actions (explain, summarize, rewrite, …) with id, label, shortLabel, icon, scope, and (by default) their prompt templates (`systemPrompt`, `userPromptTemplate`); `include_prompts: false` leaves the templates out. Templates read the text as `{text}`: the selection, or for scope `document` the document, of which the app's AI sidebar sends at most the first 8,000 characters (`doc-explain-selection` keeps its id but explains the document, as the sidebar has always sent it; its label and prompt used to say it explained a selection); `translate` and `explain-diff` also take `{arg}`, and carry an `argument` field saying what it is (the target language, or the on-disk version). No app needed. |
| `get_conversation_context` | `session_id: string`, `limit?: integer` | `{ sessionId, messages, count, recentDocs }` | Each message is `{ id, sessionId, role, content, citedDocs, timestampMs }` (`timestampMs` in milliseconds since the Unix epoch). The last N messages (default `20`, a whole number from `1` to `200`; a value outside that range is refused with `-32602`, as for `list_recent`, where one above `200` used to be clamped) of a session's memory store, oldest first. `recentDocs` lists the paths those messages cite, most recently cited first and each once (it used to be in random order). An empty or blank path that an earlier build stored is left out of `recentDocs` and of each message's own `citedDocs`. A path an earlier build stored twice in one message is listed once in that message's `citedDocs`. Empty when the session has none. A session file larger than 16 MiB is not read: the result is `isError: true` saying how large it is (it used to be read whole, and an unreadable file answered as an empty session). A `session_id` too long for its file name is refused with `-32602` (see `save_conversation_message`). |
| `save_conversation_message` | `session_id: string`, `role: "agent"\|"human"\|"system"`, `content: string`, `cited_docs?: string[]` | `{ ok, messageId, sessionId, role, timestampMs, dropped?, note? }` | Append to a session's memory store, persisted at `~/.mdopener/sessions/<session_id>.json`. ASCII letters, digits, `-` and `_` are kept in the file name and every other byte is written as `%XX`, so distinct ids never share a file (`a.b` is `a%2Eb.json`, `a_b` is `a_b.json`). That file name (without `.json`) may be at most 200 bytes, so an id of up to 200 letters, digits, `-` and `_` always fits (other bytes count three each); a longer id is refused with `-32602` instead of failing when the file is written. The sessions directory is owner-only (`0700`, tightened if an earlier build left it open) and each session file is `0600`, on Unix. Where a case-insensitive file system still folds two ids together, reads skip the other id's messages and appends are refused. History saved by earlier builds under the old name (every other character replaced by `_`) is still read, keeping only that id's messages, and the next append moves it to the new file. The Ashlr MD window persists its side of a session into the same file, in the same format (each message's `citedDocs` once per path, in the order first given, as this tool stores them), and both hold `~/.mdopener/sessions/.lock` while they update a file, so neither overwrites the other's messages. A file that cannot be parsed, or is larger than 16 MiB, is left as it is and the append is refused. A session file is kept within 16 MiB: when a message would take it past that, the oldest messages are dropped and the result says how many (`dropped`, with a `note`). A message that cannot be written to disk is not saved and returns `isError: true`. An empty or blank (whitespace-only) path in `cited_docs` is refused with `-32602` (it used to be stored and come back in `recentDocs`). Each `cited_docs` path is stored absolute: a relative one is resolved against the server's working directory when saved (it used to be stored as given), and one starting with `~/` against the home directory, and an absolute one is kept as given. A path given twice (or a relative path and its absolute form) is stored once, in the order first given (it used to be stored and returned twice). |
| `diff_documents` | `path_a: string`, `path_b: string`, `context_lines?: integer` | `{ diff, hunks, added, removed, path_a, path_b }` | Unified diff of two Markdown files on disk (non-Markdown files and dotfiles are refused). `hunks` counts the change hunks and `added` / `removed` the lines added and removed; `path_a` / `path_b` are the absolute paths read, and identical files give an empty `diff` and three zero counts. `context_lines` defaults to `3` and is a whole number from `0` to `10000`; a larger value is refused with `-32602` (it used to be read as `10000`). Lines are compared with their line endings, so files that differ only in CRLF vs LF or in the final newline are not reported as identical: a `\r` stays visible in the diff, and a last line without a newline is followed by `\ No newline at end of file`, as in `diff -u`. |
| `stream_edit` | `find: string`, `replace: string`, `preview?: boolean`, `preview_lines?: integer`, `path?: string` | `{ ok, editId, diff, candidates, matchCount, applied }` | Preview a find/replace on the open document as a unified diff (every candidate when `find` matches more than once). `diff` is the diff of the first (or only) match, `candidates` is `null` for a single match and otherwise `[{ matchIndex, startLine, diff, rank }]` in document order (rank 1 first), and `matchCount` counts the occurrences. With no document open it returns `isError: true` ("No document is open in Ashlr MD; open one first (open_file).", as `edit_document` says; it used to say that `find` was not found). A `find` that is not found (or, with `preview: false`, not unique, which the error counts: "not unique (3 matches)") or a `path` that is not the open document returns `isError: true` with the reason, and the document is unchanged; so does a preview's window that does not answer within 4 s. With `preview: false` a window that does not answer within 4 s returns `isError: true` too, but it may still apply the edit, so the error says to call `get_current_content` to see whether it did before retrying (this row used to say the document was unchanged). A refusal from the window's search also carries `matchCount` beside `content` and `isError` (the text and the rest of the result are unchanged): the occurrences of `find` it counted, `0` when it is not found. The app's `/stream-edit` reply used to drop it (`{ ok: false, error }`), and it now sends `matchCount` with them; an older app sends none, and the result then has no `matchCount`. The other refusals (no document open, a `path` that is not the open document, a busy app, a window that does not answer or fails while it handles the edit) did not search, so they carry none; the window used to send a made-up `0` for them. `preview` defaults to `true`; `false` applies immediately (not written to disk, `find` must match once) and the result has `applied: true`, an empty `diff`, `candidates: null` and an `editId` that names no preview, so do not call `stream_edit_apply` after it (a preview has `applied: false`; the row used to leave the empty `diff` unsaid). `preview_lines` defaults to `5` and is a whole number from `0` to `20`; a larger value is refused with `-32602` (it used to be read as `20`). A `path` must name the open document (compared after resolving symlinks, as `edit_document` does). Like `edit_document`, at most two edits wait on the app at once; another returns a "busy, retry" error. Prefer it over `edit_document` only to see the change before committing it: it is no cheaper for a large file, since both send the app only `find` and `replace`, a preview adds a diff and a second call, and with `path` it also asks the app for the open document's path, not its content, to compare (its description used to say to prefer it for large files, and this row that `path` fetched the whole document, which it no longer does). |
| `stream_edit_apply` | `edit_id?: string`, `find: string`, `replace: string`, `match_index?: integer`, `save?: boolean`, `path?: string` | `{ ok: true, replaced: 1, matchIndex }` | Apply a previewed `stream_edit`, choosing the occurrence with `match_index` (0-based, default `0`); `matchIndex` in the result is the occurrence applied. With no document open it returns `isError: true` ("No document is open in Ashlr MD; open one first (open_file).", as `edit_document` says) and nothing is applied or saved. A `find` no longer in the live document, a `match_index` past its last occurrence ("matchIndex 3 out of bounds: document has 2 occurrence(s). Use a match_index from 0 to 1, or call stream_edit again to see the candidates."), or a `path` that is not the open document returns `isError: true` with the reason and leaves the document unchanged, as `edit_document` does, as does a third edit while two wait on the app. A window that does not answer within 4 s returns `isError: true` too, but it may still apply the edit, so the error says to call `get_current_content` to see whether it did before retrying (this row used to count it among the refusals that leave the document unchanged). `match_index` is a whole number from `0` to `4294967295`, the app's 32-bit limit, which the schema declares as its `maximum`; a larger value is refused with `-32602` (`` `match_index` must be at most 4294967295, got … ``; it used to be refused only as "too large", with no bound in the schema). The app re-finds `find` in the live document. An empty or whitespace-only `edit_id` is refused with `-32602` (it used to be accepted). A given `edit_id` must name a preview the running app made of the open document, with the same `find` and `replace`, that has not been applied yet; a preview applies once. Otherwise the call returns `isError: true` and the document is unchanged: an unknown one (already applied, made before the app last started, or never made) says "Unknown or stale editId '<id>': ...", a preview of another document says "Stale editId '<id>': it previews '<path>', but the open document is now '<path>'.", and both end "Call stream_edit again for a fresh preview, then stream_edit_apply with its editId." (it used to be forwarded unchecked, so a stale preview re-found `find` in whatever document was open). A refusal because `find` is no longer in the live document or `match_index` is past its last occurrence also carries `matchCount` beside `content` and `isError` (the text and the rest of the result are unchanged): the occurrences of `find` the window counted. The other refusals (no document open, a `path` that is not the open document, a stale `edit_id`, a busy app, a window that does not answer) did not search, so they carry none, and neither does an older app; the app's `/stream-edit-apply` reply used to carry none at all. Without `edit_id` the apply is not checked against a preview. With the app closed the error says to start it (with `open_file`), then call `stream_edit` again for a fresh preview, since a preview from before the app started no longer exists. |
| `export_text` | `path?: string` | `{ text, word_count, char_count, path }` | Plain text of a Markdown file with the syntax stripped (code blocks kept as written, by the fence rule of `export_metadata`; code in a blockquote or a list item loses the `>` markers and the item's indentation it sits in, where list-item code used to keep its indentation; a `~~~` line inside a backtick block used to end it, and the code after it lost its `#` and `*` marks; indented code (four columns past its blockquote markers or list item text, not continuing a paragraph) is kept as code without them and its indent, where an indented line after a list item used to be read as text until the list ended, so code in an item lost its `#` and `*` marks; an item's line indented less is its continuation; and a heading loses its `#`s only by the ATX rule of `export_metadata`, so a `# comment` indented four spaces used to lose its `#`; blockquote `>` leaders are taken off before that rule, so `> # Quote` reads `Quote`, where it used to keep its `#`; each line is read past the blockquote markers, list markers and item indentation it sits in, by the container rule of the fences, so `- # Step` reads `Step` and `1)` items lose their markers, where a list item's heading used to keep its `#`): a setext heading underline (`===` or `---` after a paragraph) reads nothing, but an `===` line the page shows as text (after link reference definitions, with no paragraph before it, or lazily after a list item) is kept, where every line of only `=` or `-` used to be dropped, `~~struck~~` text keeps its words, table rows become tab-separated cells, also in a blockquote or list item (the `|---|` row is dropped, `\|` reads `|`; as in GFM and the app's own rendering, an unescaped `|` inside `` `code` `` still splits a cell), inline Markdown is read per paragraph, so a code span, inline math, emphasis or a link may run over a paragraph's line breaks (it used to be read one line at a time, so a code span over two lines kept its backticks), inline math (`$x$`, `$$x$$`, as the page's remark-math reads it) keeps its TeX without its `$`s, where its `*` and `_` used to be taken off as emphasis, and a link or image in it is none, also for `export_metadata`, footnotes read `[1]` at the reference and `[1] text` at the definition, a link reads its text and an image its alt text, without their inline marks (`[**a**](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/u)` reads `a`, where it used to keep its `**`), when its `(...)` is a CommonMark destination and title (`[t](a b)` is no link and reads as written, where it used to read `t`; a link holds no link and its text no wikilink, so `[[[W]]](u)` reads `[[W]]`, where it used to read `[W](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/u)`), but a `[text]` with no `(url)` after it keeps its brackets unless the document defines its label (`[text]: /url`), as on the page (any `[text]` used to lose them, so `[sic]` read `sic`), a link reference definition (`[text]: /url "title"`, also over two or three lines) reads nothing, as on the page, where it used to read `text: /url "title"`, an autolink reads its URL or address (`<https://x>`, `<me@x.org>`) and inline HTML reads nothing, by the CommonMark rules (an HTML tag used to be any `<` and a letter up to the next `>`, so `<me@x.org>` read nothing and `<a href="x://y">` read `a href="x://y"`), an HTML block (a `<div>` or a lone `<u>` line up to a blank line, a comment up to its `-->`) reads its text without its tags and is not read as Markdown, as the page shows it as raw HTML (a `# x` in a `<div>` used to lose its `#`, and the `===` after a `<u>` line was dropped as a setext underline), a footnote definition (`[^1]: text`) holds the lines indented four columns after it, as remark-gfm reads it, so a heading, a fence or a link reference definition in it is read as one, and `[^a b]: x` (no footnote, as its label has a space) is a link reference definition, a `<...>` link destination is read whole (`[t](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/%3Ca)b>)` reads `t`), and a wikilink reads its target, or its alias when it has one (`[[Plan|the plan]]` reads `the plan`; `[[Real]]` used to read `[Real]`, and a `![[a.png]]` embed `[a.png]`; an embed now reads nothing). The text has no blank lines before its first line or after its last, where it used to start with a line break after leading blank lines, front matter or a definition. `char_count` is the text's length in Unicode characters, not bytes. Reads `path` (Markdown only, no dotfiles) from disk, or the open document via the app when omitted (an error when nothing is open, or when the app cannot be reached; that error says to pass `path`, which needs no app). Without `path` it reads the document as the window holds it, edits not yet saved included, not its file on disk; the description used to say it operates on disk and returns the path of "the file read". |
| `export_metadata` | `path?: string` | `{ frontmatter, headings, wikilinks, wikilink_headings, embedded_image_count, word_count, path }` | Structural metadata of a Markdown file: `headings` is `[{ level, text }]`, a flat list in document order, for every ATX heading outside a leading YAML front matter block and fenced code (an empty one, `#` alone, is left out; ```` ``` ```` or `~~~`, closed only by the same character at least as long; an open fence runs to the end; a front matter `# comment` and a `# ` line after a `~~~` inside a backtick block used to be headings; a heading has at most three spaces before its `#`s, so a `# comment` indented four spaces is indented code, which used to be a heading; a heading inside a blockquote, `> # Quote`, is not listed, as in Obsidian's outline and the app's Outline panel, nor one in a list item, `- # Step` or one on an item's continuation line, `- x`, a blank line, then `  # Sub`, which used to be listed), `wikilinks` the distinct `[[link]]` targets sorted, outside fenced code by the same fence rule, indented code and code spans (a `[[link]]` in indented code or in `` `code` `` used to be listed; a front matter property such as `related: "[[Plan]]"` is a link, as Obsidian reads it; a `~~~` line inside a backtick block used to make the code after it links; a link is one line, as in Obsidian, so an unclosed `[[` no longer pairs with a `]]` lines later and hides the links between them; a target is read as the app reads it: the note without its `#heading`, so `[[Plan#Goals]]` links to `Plan`, where it used to list `Plan#Goals`, and a `]` ends no target, so `[[a]b]]` is not a link, where it used to list `a]b`; `[[#Goals]]`, a heading of the same note, has no target and is not listed), `wikilink_headings` the distinct `{ target, heading }` of each `[[target#heading]]` link, sorted by target then heading (a field added beside `wikilinks`, which keeps its shape), `embedded_image_count` the `![...](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/...)` and `![[...]]` images outside fenced and indented code, code spans and front matter (an image is one only when its `(...)` is a CommonMark destination and title, so `![a](b c)` is not; a property is not rendered, so an image in one embeds nothing; a `![[` embed is one line too, so an unclosed one is not counted), and `path` the document's absolute path (with `path` omitted, the open document's file, whose text is read from the window, edits not yet saved included, as in `export_text`). Reads `path` (Markdown only, no dotfiles) from disk, or the open document via the app when omitted (an error when nothing is open, or when the app cannot be reached; that error says to pass `path`, which needs no app). `frontmatter` is `null` when a leading `---` is never closed by `---` or `...` (that line is a thematic break, and `export_text` keeps the text after it). The supported YAML subset is described under [Front matter in `export_metadata`](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#front-matter-in-export_metadata). A leading UTF-8 byte order mark (as Notepad saves) is ignored by both `export_text` and `export_metadata`, so it does not hide the front-matter. |
| `edit_canvas` | `path: string`, `ops: object[]`, `save?: boolean` | `{ ok, path, nodes_count, edges_count, node_ids, edge_ids, removed_edge_ids, ops_applied, saved, content }` | Apply typed edit ops (move/resize/edit/color/add/delete nodes and edges, reorder edges) to a `.canvas` file, all or nothing. The extension matches in any case (`Board.CANVAS`), as Markdown extensions do (only a lowercase `.canvas` used to be taken), and a `path` that does not end in it is refused with `-32602` naming it (`` `path` must point to a .canvas file, got `notes.md` ``). `ops` must hold at least one op: an empty list is refused with `-32602` (`` `ops` must not be empty ``) before the file is read, so it is never written (the schema declares `minItems: 1`). `node_ids` / `edge_ids` are the ids left afterwards (for follow-up ops), `removed_edge_ids` the edges `delete_node` removed with their node, and `content` the new canvas JSON (a string) when `save` is `false`, which writes nothing, and `null` when the file was written. `save` defaults to `true`. Top-level keys other than `nodes` and `edges`, and unknown keys on nodes and edges, are written back unchanged; a canvas whose `nodes` or `edges` is not an array of objects is refused with `isError: true` and left untouched. Op fields are checked like arguments, before the file is read: a field of the wrong type, a field no op takes, an op without `type`, or a field shorter than its declared `minLength` (an op's empty `id` or `ids` element) is refused with `-32602` naming the op and field (`` `ops[1].x` must be a number ``, `` `ops[0].id` must be at least 1 character long ``). So is a field that another op takes but this op does not use (`width` on a `move_node`, which used to be ignored while the call reported success): the error names the ops that use it, and a move and a resize are two ops. An empty or whitespace-only id (an op's `id`, an element of `reorder_edges`' `ids`, `add_node`'s `node.id`, or `add_edge`'s `edge.id`, `edge.fromNode` or `edge.toNode`) is refused with `-32602` before the file is read (`` op[0] move_node: `id` must not be empty ``; it used to come back as "node `` not found"). `move_node` and `resize_node` write a whole-number `x`, `y`, `width` or `height` as a JSON integer, as JSON Canvas expects (`5` or `5.0` is written `5`; it used to be written `5.0`), and a fractional one as given. `add_node` refuses (`-32602`) a node the app would not show: it needs a non-empty string `id`, a `type` of `text`, `file`, `link` or `group`, numbers `x`, `y`, `width` and `height` (size positive), a string `file` for a file node and `url` for a link node. `add_edge` likewise refuses (`-32602`) an edge whose `fromSide`/`toSide` is not `top`, `right`, `bottom` or `left`, whose `fromEnd`/`toEnd` is not `none` or `arrow`, or whose `label` is not a string (these used to be written as given). A color (`set_node_color`'s `color`, `add_node`'s `node.color`, `add_edge`'s `edge.color`) must be what JSON Canvas allows, a preset `"1"`..`"6"` or a hex `#rgb` / `#rrggbb`; anything else (`"red"`, `"7"`) is refused with `-32602`. A node or edge id that is not in the canvas (in `move_node`, `delete_edge`, `add_edge`'s `fromNode`/`toNode`, `reorder_edges` and the rest) is refused with `-32602` listing the ids that exist at that op, after the ops before it (the first 20, then a count), and saying the file was left unchanged (`` op[0] move_node: node `n2` not found. The canvas's node ids at this op are `n1`, `n3`. No op was applied and the file was left unchanged. ``); it used to name only the missing id. It is listed with `destructiveHint: true`, among the destructive tools after the read-only and targeted ones: it writes the canvas back in place (`save` defaults to `true`) and can remove nodes and edges, and it used to say `false`, so a client that confirms destructive tools let it rewrite a canvas unasked. |
| `export` | `format: "pdf"\|"docx"\|"html"\|"epub"`, `output_path?: string`, `overwrite?: boolean` | `{ ok, format, path, bytes }` or `{ ok, format, dialog: true }` | Export the open document. With none open it is `isError` naming the next step ("No document is open to export. Call open_file with the document's `path` and mode "read", then retry."; it used to say only "open one before exporting"). With `output_path` (html, docx or epub, with that extension, in an existing directory) the app writes the file without a dialog and the call returns once the window reports it written and it is on disk. An export that fails in the window returns `isError` at once with the window's reason; from Edit or Source view that reason says to call `open_file` with the document's path and `mode: "read"`, then retry (it used to be "Switch to Read view before exporting.", a toggle only the human can click); one the window has not finished within 30 s returns `isError` saying so. The app writes one headless export at a time, in a slot of its own, so a slow export never makes edits, opens, presents or reviews wait; a second headless export sent while one is being written returns `isError` at once saying so (retry once the first finishes). The document must be in Read view. Without `output_path` the app opens its export dialog. pdf goes through the system print dialog and takes no `output_path`. Exports use the app's current theme; a `theme` argument is refused (`-32602`). A file already at `output_path` is replaced only with `overwrite: true` (default `false`): without it the call returns `isError` saying it exists, and nothing is written or sent to the app. A file that appears after that check is not replaced either: the app is told not to replace one, and writes the export to a temp file published with a hard link (or created with `O_EXCL` where links are not supported), which fails when anything is at the path, so the call returns `isError` saying a file is already there. The check and the write used to be two steps. It is listed with `destructiveHint: true`, after the read-only and targeted tools; it used to say `false` and overwrote the file unasked. |
| `replace_document` | `content: string`, `save?: boolean` | `{ ok: true }` | Replace the **entire** content of the open document, the same operation as `set_content`. Prefer `edit_document` for targeted changes. In a CRLF document (one with `\r\n` and no lone `\n`) a `content` with no `\r` takes CRLF line breaks, and a document that starts with a byte order mark keeps it when `content` has none. Refuses with no document open and reports a failed apply or save as `set_content` does. |
| `set_content` | `content: string`, `save?: boolean` | `{ ok: true }` | Replace the **entire** content of the open document, the same operation as `replace_document`, and like it listed with `destructiveHint: true`. `save` defaults to `false`. The call returns `{ ok: true }` once the window has applied the content (and saved it, with `save: true`). With no document open it returns `isError: true` ("No document is open in Ashlr MD; open one first (open_file).") and nothing is applied. The app opens only files (with none it shows its welcome screen), so every document it shows has one, and there is no unsaved document to fill: the description used to promise a "replaced but not saved" result for "a document with no file yet", which never came. With `save: true`, a save that fails returns `isError: true` saying the content was replaced but not saved (the buffer keeps the new content), and a window that does not answer within 4 s returns `isError: true` saying it may still apply the content, and to call `get_current_content` to see whether it did before retrying. Like `edit_document`, at most two edits wait on the app at once; another returns a "busy, retry" error. A `content` larger than the 16 MiB the app reads in one request (counted with JSON escapes) is refused with `-32602` before it is sent, as for `replace_document`, `edit_document`, `stream_edit`, `stream_edit_apply` and `request_review` (see the paragraphs below this table). |

Every path argument (`path`, `path_a`, `path_b`, `vault`, `output_path` and
each `cited_docs` entry) may be absolute, relative to the server's working
directory, or start with `~/` (or be `~` alone) for the home directory, as in
a shell. A leading `~` used to be read as a folder named `~` in the working
directory, so `~/notes/plan.md` came back as a file that does not exist.
`~user` and a `~` later in the path are kept as given.

A document a tool reads from disk must be UTF-8 text. One that is not (a
Latin-1 or UTF-16 file, as some Windows editors save) is `isError: true`
naming the first byte that is not valid UTF-8 and its line (or saying it is
UTF-16), and saying to convert the file to UTF-8; it used to say only "stream
did not contain valid UTF-8". The app gives the same reason when it reads
the file itself, so `open_file`, `present_document` and `request_review` (with
`path`) of such a file fail with it too, and so does the window's own open
and a patch the human applies to the file.

The app reads at most 16 MiB of one request. A call that would send it more
(`set_content` or `replace_document` with a larger `content`, `edit_document`,
`stream_edit` or `stream_edit_apply` with a larger `find` and `replace`, or
`request_review` with a larger inline `content`), measured as sent, with JSON
escapes, is refused with `-32602` before anything is sent, saying what to do
instead: change part of the document with `edit_document`, split the edit,
or pass the review text as a file's `path`. It used to be sent, and the app's
refusal reached the agent as "IPC write error: Connection reset by peer".

When a tool fails while running (the app is not running, a file cannot be read
or written, the app rejects the operation), the call still succeeds at the
JSON-RPC level and returns `isError: true` with the reason as text, as the MCP
spec asks, so the agent sees the message and can act on it. JSON-RPC errors
are reserved for protocol problems: an unknown tool or invalid arguments
(`-32602`).

Arguments are checked against the tool's `inputSchema` before it runs. An
argument the schema does not declare (a typo such as `pth`), a value of the
wrong JSON type (`"limit": "5"`, `"include_prompts": "no"`, a number inside
`cited_docs`) or `arguments` that is not an object is refused with `-32602`
naming the argument; an undeclared one also lists the arguments the tool
takes and the closest match. Every integer argument declares a `minimum` in
its schema (`0`, or `1` for the `limit` of `search_vault`, `list_recent` and
`get_conversation_context`, and for `request_review` the `5000` of
`timeout_ms` and the `1000` of `wait_ms`), and a value
below it (`"limit": -5`, `"match_index": -1`) is refused the same way instead
of falling back to the default. An integer above its declared `maximum`
(the `limit` of `search_vault`, `list_recent` and `get_conversation_context` declares `200`, `diff_documents`' `context_lines` `10000`, `stream_edit`'s `preview_lines` `20`, `stream_edit_apply`'s `match_index` `4294967295`, and `request_review`'s
`timeout_ms` and `wait_ms` `600000`) is refused the same way. A string outside the property's `enum`
(`"mode": "view"`, `"role": "bot"`, an `edit_canvas` op `type` of
`"move"`) is refused the same way, and the message lists the allowed values
(`` `mode` must be one of `read`, `edit`, got a string ("view") ``). A string
shorter than the property's `minLength` is refused the same way. Every
required string a tool cannot use when empty declares `1`: `search_vault`'s
`query`, `edit_document`'s and `stream_edit`'s and `stream_edit_apply`'s
`find`, `get_user_annotations`'s and `edit_canvas`'s `path`, and the
`session_id` of both conversation tools and `save_conversation_message`'s
`content`. So does every path a tool reads or opens (`open_file`'s,
`present_document`'s, `export_text`'s, `export_metadata`'s and
`request_review`'s `path`, `diff_documents`' `path_a` and `path_b`),
`request_review`'s inline `content` and `search_vault`'s `vault`, and
the optional `path` of `edit_document`, `stream_edit` and
`stream_edit_apply`, `stream_edit_apply`'s `edit_id` and `export`'s
`output_path` (omitting them is still allowed): an empty one, or one of only
whitespace, is refused with `-32602`
(`` `path` must not be empty ``), where it used to reach the file checks and
come back as "only Markdown documents can be read", "No such file or
directory", "not the open document" or "cannot make an empty path
absolute". `search_vault` also refuses a `query` that is
only whitespace with `-32602`, before it asks the app (it used to report that
the app was not running). So a string such as `"1"`, a negative or a
fractional `match_index` is refused rather than read as `0`, and `"save":
"true"` rather than read as `false`. A whole number written as a float
(`2.0`) is an integer, as in JSON Schema. `null` counts as not given. A
`required` argument that is missing (or `null`) is refused the same way
(`` `ops` is required ``) before the tool reads anything, and `request_review`
without any of `path`, `content` or `review_id` is refused naming all three.
A test drives every tool's advertised schema through this check, so the
schema's `required` list, property types and `enum` values are what is enforced. An unknown tool
name gets the closest tool name, if any, and a pointer to `tools/list`. A
blank `session_id` is refused like a missing one. `prompts/get` with an
unknown or missing `name` and `resources/read` with an unknown or missing
`uri` answer `-32602` the same way: the closest prompt or URI, if any, and
the prompt names or a pointer to `resources/list`.

### `edit_document`: exact, unique find/replace

`edit_document` replaces an **exact substring** of the currently open document.
The `find` string must occur **exactly once**:

- **0 matches** → the edit is refused: *"`find` string not found in the current document."*
- **2+ matches** → the edit is refused: *"`find` string is not unique (N matches): include more surrounding context to disambiguate."*
- **empty `find`** → refused by the MCP server itself with `-32602` (*"`find` must not be empty"*), whether or not the app is running.
