Matching is exact except for line breaks: a line break in `find` (`\n` or
`\r\n`) matches either in the document, so an LF `find` edits a CRLF file
(it used to be "not found" there), and `replace` is written in the line breaks
of the line the match starts on, so a CRLF file keeps CRLF lines and a mixed
file keeps each part's. The same holds for `stream_edit` and
`stream_edit_apply`. A byte order mark and the text around the match are left
as they are.

So include enough surrounding context to make `find` unique. These soft failures
come back as a **tool error** (`isError: true`) with the reason, not an opaque
transport failure, so the agent can retry with more context.

Pass `path` to assert which file is open: if a *different* document is currently
open, the edit is refused rather than silently applied to the wrong file. Pass
`save: true` to persist to disk immediately (default `false`: edits stay in the
live buffer until saved).

### `request_review`: blocking human sign-off

See the dedicated [Human review loop](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#human-review-loop) section.

### Front matter in `export_metadata`

The block opens on a first line of `---` and closes on a later `---` or
`...` line. Each delimiter starts at column 0 with only spaces or tabs after
it, as the app's renderer reads front matter, so `  ---` is a thematic break
and opens no block (the line used to be trimmed, which hid the text up to the
next `---` from the headings, tasks and `export_text`).

`frontmatter` reads a small subset of YAML, not full YAML:

- **Scalars**: `true` / `false` become booleans, integers and decimals become
  numbers, `~`, `null` and an empty value (`key:` with nothing after it and
  nothing under it) become `null`, and anything else is a string with
  surrounding `"` or `'` removed (`key: ""` is the empty string).
- **Lists**: a flow list (`tags: [a, "b, c"]`) or `- item` lines under an
  empty `key:` become arrays. An item written as `- name: x` starts an object,
  and the lines aligned with `name` add keys to it, so
  `- name: Ann` / `  role: lead` is `{"name": "Ann", "role": "lead"}`. An item
  in quotes, or whose colons are not followed by a space (`- http://x`), stays
  a string.
- **Nesting**: indented `name: value` lines under an empty `owner:` become an
  object (`{"owner": {"name": "value"}}`), at any depth. Their values are read
  the same way, so `links: [a, b]` or `- item` lines under `roles:` are
  arrays, and an empty one is `null`.
- **Block scalars**: `key: |` keeps the indented lines under it as written,
  and `key: >` folds them: a line break between two lines becomes a space, a
  blank line becomes a line break, and lines indented further keep their
  breaks. Both end with one line break; `|-` / `>-` drop it and `|+` / `>+`
  keep every trailing blank line. An explicit indentation digit (`|2`) is
  honoured. Lines inside a block scalar are text, so `# ...` there is kept.
- A key's colon must be followed by a space or end the line, so `time: 10:30`
  is the string `"10:30"`.
- **Not parsed**: anchors and aliases (`&a`, `*a`), tags (`!!str`), flow
  mappings (`{a: 1}` stays a string), and multi-line plain or quoted scalars
  (their continuation lines are skipped). Comment lines (`# ...`) outside
  block scalars are skipped.

---

## Resources reference

The server implements `resources/list`, `resources/templates/list` and
`resources/read`. `resources/templates/list` offers one template,
`text://vault-search?q={query}` (`mimeType: application/json`), the search
below. Listing it needs no app; reading it needs the app unless `&vault=` is
given (this used to say only "it needs no app"). The `resources/list` entry
names the same parameters, `&limit=` included (it used to leave `limit` out).

- **`mdopener://current`**: the document currently open in Ashlr MD
  (`mimeType: text/markdown`). Reading it returns the live content; an open
  document that is empty is `""`. With no document open (the app answers
  `path: null`, whatever its `content`) it is `-32002` ("No document is
  open"), as for the prompts. It is `-32000` when the app is not running,
  and also when the app answers HTTP 401 (it refuses this server's token),
  with the refused-token message (see [Troubleshooting](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md#troubleshooting))
  instead of the not-running one. Any other HTTP error the app answers (a
  404 or a 500) is `-32000` too, with the app's reason as the message (a
  500 whose reason said "not found" used to read as a closed app).
- **`text://vault-search?q=<query>`**: the same search as `search_vault`, as a
  resource (`mimeType: application/json`; optional `&limit=`, `&vault=` and
  `&semantic=false` or `true` to force grep or semantic search, like
  `search_vault`'s `semantic`; any other value, a `limit` that is not a
  whole number from 1 to 200, a parameter with no value, or any other
  parameter (a misspelt `lmit=5`) is `-32602`, naming the closest one; so
  is a parameter given twice (`q=a&q=b` used to search for `b` alone) and a
  malformed escape (`q=%ZZ` used to search for the literal `%ZZ`; write a
  literal `%` as `%25`, a `+` as `%2B`)).
  Returns `{ results, mode, query, note?, vault?, truncated?, depthCut? }`,
  with the same `note`, `truncated` and `depthCut` as `search_vault` when it
  fell back or did not search every file; an error when the app is not
  running and no `vault` is given.
- **`mdopener://recent-documents`**: recently opened files that still exist,
  each with `path`, `title`, `mtimeMs`, and a 200-character `preview`
  (`mimeType: application/json`), as `{ documents, count, skipped }`.
  `title` is the text of the first level 1 ATX heading outside YAML front
  matter, fenced code blocks, blockquotes and list items (one on a list
  item's continuation line, `- x`, a blank line, then `  # Sub`, used to
  be the title), else the file name without its extension
  (a `# ` line in front matter or a code block used to be taken as the
  title). A heading has at most three spaces before its `#` and a space, a
  tab or the end of the line after it, and its closing `#`s are dropped, as
  in CommonMark and `export_metadata`'s headings; only `# ` at the start of
  a line used to count, so `  # Title` and `#<tab>Title` were not titles.
  Recents that cannot be listed are left out and counted in `skipped` by
  reason: `missing` (no longer on disk), `notDocument` (a dotfile, not
  Markdown, or not a regular file), `tooLarge` (past 16 MiB) and
  `unreadable` (any other read failure, such as text that is not UTF-8).
  An app with no recents gives an empty list;
  an app that cannot be reached, that refuses this server's token (HTTP
  401) or that answers any other HTTP error is `-32000`, as for
  `mdopener://current` (it used to be an empty list too).
- **`file://<path>` (vault files)**: every file the app lists in the
  **vault** (watched folder) is listed as an individually readable resource.
  The path in the URI is percent-encoded as RFC 3986 and RFC 8089 require:
  every byte but a letter, a digit, `-._~`, `!$&'()*+,;=`, `:`, `@` and the
  `/` separator is written `%XX`, so `/notes/My Notes 100%.md` is listed as
  `file:///notes/My%20Notes%20100%25.md` and `café.md` as `caf%C3%A9.md`. A
  Windows path `C:\notes\a.md` is `file:///C:/notes/a.md`, and a share
  `\\srv\share\a.md` is `file:////srv/share/a.md`. The URIs used to be
  `file://` followed by the path as is, which is not a valid URI when the
  path has a space; `resources/read` still takes that form.
  Recently opened files are not listed as `file://` entries (read
  `mdopener://recent-documents` for them), but a recent's `file://<path>` is
  still readable through `resources/read`. When the app cannot be asked for them (it is not
  running, or it refused), the list has none, and the result carries
  `_meta: { "mdopener/vaultFilesUnlisted": "<reason>" }` (also logged on
  stderr) so a client can tell that from a vault with no files; a listing
  that worked has no such key. When the app's vault list is cut short (the
  watched folder has more Markdown files than the app lists, or is too large
  or too deeply nested to scan in full, as `search_vault`'s `truncated`
  says), the result carries `_meta: { "mdopener/vaultFilesTruncated":
  "<reason>" }`, naming the app's cap, so the `file://` entries are not
  read as the whole vault.

`resources/read` is **scoped**: a `file://` URI is only readable if it is one of
the paths the app currently advertises in the vault or recents. Any other path
is rejected (`-32002`, saying to open it with `open_file` first), so the resource channel can't be used as an
arbitrary-filesystem read primitive. When the app cannot be reached it lists
no path, and the read is `-32000` saying the app is not running, or with
the refused-token message when the app answers HTTP 401, as for
`mdopener://current` (it used to be `-32002` "not in vault"). The
percent-encoded URIs `resources/list` gives (`file:///notes/My%20Notes.md`),
the same path written unencoded (`file:///notes/My Notes.md`, the form it
used to give, tried first) and `file://localhost/...` are accepted, and a
`file:///C:/...` or `file:////srv/share/...` URI names the Windows path the
app lists; the check runs on the decoded path, so encoding cannot reach a
file outside the vault. A malformed escape (`%ZZ`, a lone `%`; write a literal `%` as `%25`) or
escapes that do not decode to UTF-8 (`%FF`) are refused with `-32602` naming
the problem, unless the URI is an advertised path exactly as written. An advertised path is then read only if it is a Markdown document that
is not a dotfile, checked after resolving symlinks (like the tools that read a
path from disk), so a vault `notes.md` that links to `~/.ssh/id_rsa` or `.env`
is refused (`-32002`). `mdopener://recent-documents` skips such a recent
instead of previewing its target.

---

## Prompts reference

The server implements `prompts/list` and `prompts/get`. Each prompt embeds the
**live document** so the returned message is self-contained:

| Prompt | What it asks the model to do |
|---|---|
| `summarize` | Summarize the current document into a short bulleted list of key points. |
| `review_plan` | Review the current document as an implementation plan; flag risks, missing steps, and anything ambiguous. |
| `improve_writing` | Tighten the prose and fix grammar of the current document without changing its meaning or structure. |

`prompts/get` returns a single `user` message whose text is the instruction
followed by the current document content. With no document open it is
`-32002` ("No document is open"), and `-32000` when the app is not running
or answers HTTP 401 (it refuses this server's token, and the message says
how to fix it), the same errors `mdopener://current` gives; any other
HTTP error the app answers is `-32000` too, with the app's reason as the
message. No prompt takes arguments: `arguments` may be left out, `null` or
`{}`, and any argument given (such as a `path`, which used to be dropped
while the prompt ran on the open document) is refused with `-32602`; open
the document you mean with `open_file` first. Each prompt's `prompts/list`
description says so too, `-32000` included (it used to name only a closed
app).

---

## Human review loop

`request_review` is the heart of the agent-with-a-human-in-the-loop workflow. It
lets an agent stop and get **explicit human sign-off** on a plan, diff, or doc
before proceeding.

### Flow

1. **Agent calls `request_review`** with either a file `path` or inline
   `content`. The MCP server registers the review with the app (a unique
   `reviewId` is generated) and, if a `path` was given, opens that file in read
   mode. The app shows its **review panel**. If the app cannot open the file,
   no review is registered and the call returns `isError: true` with the
   app's reason.
2. **The call BLOCKS** (when `blocking` is `true`, the default). Under the hood
   the MCP binary polls the app every ~1.5s for a verdict, for at most
   `wait_ms` (default 50 s, below the 60 s request timeout of common MCP
   clients). If the human has not decided by then it returns
   `{ "status": "pending", "reviewId": "…" }`; call `request_review` again with
   `review_id` to keep waiting on the same review.
3. **The human acts in the app**, clicking **Approve**, **Request changes**, or
   **Dismiss**, optionally leaving comments.
4. **The agent receives the verdict** as the tool result:
   `{ "verdict": "approved" | "changes_requested" | "dismissed", "reviewId": "…", "comments": "…" }`.
   `dismissed` means the human closed the panel. If the panel's countdown runs
   out with no decision, the verdict is `timeout`. A `timeout` never replaces
   a verdict already given. If the human still decides after the window has
   closed (an agent may already have been told `timeout`), that verdict is
   recorded with `"late": true` and a `message` saying so, in the
   `request_review` result of a resumed call and in `get_user_annotations`.
5. **One review at a time.** The panel shows a single review. When another
   `request_review` (from this agent or another) reaches the panel before the
   human has decided, the review it replaces ends at once with
   `{ "verdict": "superseded", "reviewId": "…", "supersededBy": "…", "message": "…" }`
   (also when resumed with `review_id`, and in `get_user_annotations`), rather
   than waiting out its window and reporting `timeout`. Call `request_review`
   again if it still needs sign-off. Reviews are not queued: a queued review's
   window would run out while it is hidden, and the human sees the newest
   request, which is usually the one that matters. A verdict the human was
   already submitting as the panel switched is still recorded, marked `late`.

### Parameters

- `path` *or* `content`: **one is required.** `path` opens that file for review;
  `content` reviews inline Markdown, which the review panel shows as text
  (it used to show only "inline content", so the human never saw what they
  were approving).
- `blocking` (default `true`): if `false`, the review is registered and the call
  returns immediately with `{ "reviewId": "…", "status": "pending", "message": "…" }`.
  Call `request_review` with that `review_id` to wait for the verdict. A
  resumed call with `blocking: false` does not wait: it reads the review once
  and returns its verdict, `{ "status": "pending", … }`, or `timeout` once its
  window has closed, ignoring `wait_ms`. A
  review of a `path` can also be read later via `get_user_annotations`; one
  of inline `content` has no path, so only `review_id` finds it.
- `timeout_ms` (default `300000` = 5 min, must be **5 000 to 600 000**): how long
  the human has to decide (the review panel's window). A value outside that
  range (or not a whole number) is refused with an invalid-params error naming
  the range, and no review is registered; the app's `/review` refuses the same
  values with a 400. When the window closes
  during a call (the first one, or one resumed with `review_id`) with no
  decision, the tool returns `{ "verdict": "timeout", … }`, so resuming a
  review never waits past its window.
- `wait_ms` (default `50000`, must be **1 000 to 600 000**): the most one call
  blocks. Raise it only if your client allows longer tool calls. A value
  outside that range (or not a whole number) is refused with an
  invalid-params error naming the range, and no review is registered; it
  used to be clamped in silence. To return without waiting, pass
  `blocking: false`.
- `review_id`: resume waiting on a review an earlier call returned as pending
  (no new review is registered). An empty or blank `review_id` is refused with
  `-32602`; it used to be read as absent, so the call registered a new review
  that replaced the pending one. A resumed call cannot change the review, so
  `path`, `content` and `timeout_ms` may be resent unchanged (or left out), and
  one that differs from what the review was requested with is refused with an
  invalid-params error naming it, and nothing is waited on. Refusing, rather
  than going ahead and noting it, is deliberate: an agent that changed its
  `content` and kept the old `review_id` would otherwise read the human's
  verdict on the old text as a verdict on the new one. The server remembers
  the last 256 reviews it registered; for a review it did not register (it was
  restarted, or another server registered it) nothing can be compared, so the
  call goes ahead and the result lists those arguments as `ignored`, with a
  `note`. Once its `timeout_ms` window has closed with
  no verdict, the call returns `{ "verdict": "timeout", … }`.
  The app keeps a review for 30 minutes after its `timeout_ms` window closes,
  so resume within that time; later the call returns `verdict: "timeout"`
  (the record is gone). The newest review of each file is kept longer, for
  `get_user_annotations`, and the app holds at most 256 reviews, dropping the
  oldest decided ones first.

### Reading the result later

`get_user_annotations(path)` returns the **latest** verdict and comments recorded
for a file (with `late: true` when that verdict came after its review window
closed), plus the current state of its GFM task checkboxes
(`- [ ]` / `- [x]`, including `*`/`+` bullets). Use it after a non-blocking
`request_review`, or to re-check whether the human has ticked off task items.

When Ashlr MD is not running, `get_user_annotations` still answers, from
disk: `tasks` are the checkboxes saved in the file, and `verdict`, `comments`
and `late` are the last review the app saved for that file in
`~/.mdopener/reviews/` (`null` when none was saved), with `appRunning: false`
and a `note`. The app saves a review of a file there when it is decided or
superseded: one owner-only (`0600`, folder `0700`) JSON file per document,
at most 256 KiB, written atomically; a newer review of the same file always
wins, and a file that is oversized, corrupt, or names another path is
ignored. A saved review adds `saved: true`, `reviewId`, `reviewedAt` (ms
since the epoch), `supersededBy` for a superseded review, and `stale`. `stale`
is `true` when the file changed since the review (its content hash differs) or
cannot be compared: the verdict was for an earlier version, so a stale
`approved` is not approval of the file as it is now, and the `note` says to
call `request_review` (`open_file` starts the app) to ask again. A review of
inline content (no path) is not saved. A file
that cannot be read (missing, not a Markdown document, or larger than 16 MiB)
has empty `tasks` and a `tasksNote` saying why, in the words the other disk
tools use (for a missing file, "Cannot read '/abs/plan.md': the file does not
exist. Its tasks were not read."). An app that answers HTTP 401
(it refused the token in `~/.mdopener/ipc-token`: the file is stale, or the
port belongs to another Ashlr MD instance) is read from disk the same way, but
the result has `appAuthFailed: true` instead of `appRunning`, and its `note`
says to ask the user to quit every Ashlr MD window and start the app again
(which writes a new port and token), then call `get_user_annotations` again.
Any other error from the app is still an error.

### Tips for agents

- Use `request_review` for **gates**: "Here's the plan / the diff / the final
  doc. Approve before I continue."
- Pair it with `present_document` when you want the human to read a polished
  result without the app's chrome, then call `request_review` for the sign-off.
- On `changes_requested`, read the returned `comments`, apply fixes with
  `edit_document`, and request review again.

---

## Auto-open hook

`mdopen --hook` is a Claude Code **PostToolUse hook**: whenever Claude writes or
edits a Markdown file, the file auto-opens in Ashlr MD for review. The hook is
silent and exits `0`, so it never disrupts Claude's tool flow: it reads
the PostToolUse JSON from stdin, extracts the written file path, and opens it in
read mode: through the running app's loopback IPC channel, or via the
`mdopener://` scheme when the app is not running. It reads at most 64 MiB of
stdin; a longer payload opens nothing (still silently, exit `0`). It acts only
on a `PostToolUse` payload from `Write`, `Edit` or `MultiEdit`: a payload whose
`hook_event_name` is another event (a hook wired as `PreToolUse` would open the
file before the tool changed it) or whose `tool_name` is another tool (`Read`
carries a `file_path` too) opens nothing, so a broad hand-written matcher does
not open every Markdown file the agent reads. A payload whose `tool_response`
reports the tool failed (`success: false`, `is_error: true`, a non-empty
`error`, or a `<tool_use_error>` string) opens nothing either, since a failed
`Edit` leaves the file unchanged. A payload without those fields is judged by
its `tool_input.file_path` alone. The hook command takes no arguments besides
`--hook`: `mdopen --hook notes.md` is a usage error (exit `1`, naming the
extra argument on stderr, which Claude Code reports without blocking the
tool call), since the payload arrives on stdin.

### One-click install

**Preferences → AI agents (MCP) → Auto-open agent Markdown**. Ashlr MD merges this
into **`~/.claude/settings.json`** (idempotently: it won't add a duplicate).
If the hook it installed earlier runs an `mdopen` that no longer exists (the app
was moved, for example from Downloads to Applications), clicking it again points
the hook at this copy of the app; a hook running another `mdopen` that exists is
left alone:

```json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PostToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Edit|Write",
        "hooks": [
          {
            "type": "command",
            "command": "'<mdopen>' --hook",
            "if": "Write(*.md)|Edit(*.md)"
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

The `matcher` fires on the `Edit` and `Write` tools; the `if` guard narrows it to
`*.md` files. The `mdopen` path is single-quoted so the space in "Ashlr MD" does
not split it; re-running the installer repairs an unquoted entry that earlier
versions wrote for the same path. After installing, **restart Claude Code** to
pick it up. The quoting targets the POSIX shell Claude Code runs hooks with; it
has not been verified on an installed Windows build.

From an AppImage the button does not write the `mdopen` inside the
AppImage's temporary mount (`/tmp/.mount_*`), which is gone once the app
quits: it copies `mdopen` to `~/.local/share/app.mdopener.desktop/bin/mdopen`
and writes that path, refreshing the copy when you click it again after
updating the AppImage.

> If `~/.claude/settings.json` already has a non-object `hooks` value or a
> non-array `hooks.PostToolUse`, the installer **bails with an error** rather than
> clobbering your settings; fix the shape manually and retry.

---

## The `mdopen` CLI

`mdopen` opens any Markdown file in Ashlr MD from a terminal, CI script, or agent
tool call.
When the app is running, `mdopen` hands it the file over the token-authenticated
loopback IPC channel, so it works even where the `mdopener://` scheme is not
registered (an AppImage or dev build on Linux). Otherwise it opens the
`mdopener://` URL, which launches the app. It exits `1` when neither works;
for `mdopen -` the temp file holding stdin is then removed. The message names
the file, what the running-app route and the `mdopener://` route each hit,
and ends with the next step (start Ashlr MD, then run `mdopen` again). It also
exits `1`, before contacting the app, for a file that is not a Markdown document
(`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd`, `.mdx`) or is a dotfile, checked after
symlinks are resolved; and when the running app refuses the file, it exits `1`
with the app's reason on stderr without trying the URL scheme. It also exits
`1` without trying the URL scheme when the running app was reached but
failed: it answered with a server error, the connection broke, or it did not
answer within 6 s. The app may still open the file then, so for `mdopen -`
the temp file is kept. When the running app refuses the token (HTTP 401),
`mdopen` still tries the `mdopener://` URL, and if that opens the file it
exits `0` but prints the stale-token problem and its fix to stderr ("IPC auth
failed: Ashlr MD refused the token in ~/.mdopener/ipc-token (HTTP 401), ...;
quit every Ashlr MD window and start it again, which writes a new token. The
file was opened through the mdopener:// URL instead."), as it reports an
unconfirmed launch; it used to say nothing, so the stale token went unnoticed.
`--hook` stays silent. `mdopen -` also
exits `1`, opening nothing, when stdin is empty or only whitespace, or longer
than the 16 MiB a document may be (it stops reading there and writes no temp
file). Run with a
terminal on stdin (nothing piped), it prints how to finish typing (Ctrl+D, or
Ctrl+Z and Enter on Windows) to stderr. Run with no arguments at all, it prints its help to stderr and exits
`1`; `mdopen --help` prints it to stdout and exits `0`. An empty or blank
path (`mdopen "$FILE"` with an empty variable) is a usage error saying the
path is empty, and a directory is refused as a directory (exit `1` for
both). An argument that is
not valid UTF-8 is a usage error (exit `1`, naming it on stderr): Ashlr MD
takes paths as UTF-8 text, and such an argument used to crash `mdopen` with
exit `101`, `--hook` included.

### Install

In Ashlr MD: **Preferences → Command-line tool → Install mdopen** (all platforms).
From an AppImage, the link it makes points at the copy of `mdopen` in
`~/.local/share/app.mdopener.desktop/bin/`, not inside the AppImage's mount.

Or via the build-from-source installer (macOS/Linux):

```bash
bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/main/scripts/install.sh)
```

On **Windows**, the app installer places `mdopen.exe` alongside the app, and
**Install mdopen** copies it to `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\mdopen.exe`. Neither
folder is on `PATH` by default, so add one of them to your user `PATH` yourself.

### Usage

```bash
mdopen README.md                # open a file (read mode, default)
mdopen --edit PLAN.md           # open directly in edit mode (-e also works)
mdopen --read NOTES.md          # force read mode (-r also works; with --edit it is a usage error)
cat notes.md | mdopen -         # pipe stdin → temp file → open in app
mdopen -- -draft.md             # `--` ends flags, for file names starting with `-`
mdopen -- -                     # after `--`, `-` is a file named `-`, not stdin
mdopen --hook                   # Claude Code PostToolUse hook mode (reads JSON on stdin)
mdopen --help                   # print usage (-h also works); wins over every other flag, --hook included
mdopen --version                # print the version (-V also works)
```

### From an agent

Claude Code (and other agents with shell access) can call `mdopen` directly:

```python
# In a Python agent tool
import subprocess
subprocess.run(["mdopen", "/path/to/output.md"], check=True)
```

---

## The `mdopener://` URL scheme

Any app (browser, terminal, script) can open a file in Ashlr MD via the custom
URL scheme:

```
mdopener://open?path=/absolute/path/to/file.md
mdopener://open?path=/path/to/file.md&mode=edit
```

From the terminal:

```bash
# macOS
open "mdopener://open?path=$(pwd)/README.md"

# Windows (PowerShell)
Start-Process "mdopener://open?path=$PWD\README.md"

# Linux
xdg-open "mdopener://open?path=$(pwd)/README.md"
```

From JavaScript / Electron:

```js
shell.openExternal(`mdopener://open?path=${encodeURIComponent(filePath)}`);
```

Since any web page or program can launch these links, a link opens only an
existing Markdown document that is not a dotfile (checked after resolving
symlinks, as for `open_file`); anything else is ignored. The `path` is
percent-decoded once. `mode` is `read` or `edit` and switches the document
to that view once it is open, also when the link starts the app (so does
`mdopen --edit` with the app closed); a link with any other `mode` is
ignored, as `open_file` refuses one. `mode` used to be dropped, so the file
opened in whatever view it was. Other parameters are ignored, by open and
export links alike, and of a parameter given twice the first counts.

`mdopener://export?path=<path>&format=pdf|docx|html|epub` opens the file and,
once it has loaded (also when the link starts the app), the export dialog
with that format selected (`format` defaults to `pdf`). The export request
used to be sent with the open, so a link that started the app only opened
the file. An export link always switches the file to Read view, which
exporting needs: `mode` may be left out or be `read`, and a link with
`mode=edit` (or any value an open link refuses) is ignored. It used to
ignore `mode` and export from whatever view the file was in, which fails in
Edit view. A link with any other `format` (`PDF`, `md`) is ignored, as the
`export` tool refuses one; it used to open the dialog with no format
selected.

---

## How it works: the IPC model

The MCP binary communicates with the running Ashlr MD app over a **loopback HTTP
server** bound to `127.0.0.1` on an OS-assigned port. On startup the app writes
its port to `~/.mdopener/ipc-port` and a per-session token to
`~/.mdopener/ipc-token`; the MCP binary reads both to locate and authenticate to
the app, and the app removes them on clean exit.

If the app is not running, most tools return a clear error; `open_file` is the
exception and will cold-start the app via the `mdopener://` URL scheme. The
frontend keeps the app's document, recents, and vault state mirrored to the IPC
layer (via `mcp_sync_state` / `mcp_sync_vault`) so reads are always fresh without
re-walking the disk.

---

## Security

The integration is **local-only and token-authenticated**:

- The IPC server binds to **`127.0.0.1`** (loopback) on an ephemeral port, so
  nothing is exposed beyond your machine.
- On startup the app generates a **32-byte CSPRNG token** (64 hex chars) and
  writes it to `~/.mdopener/ipc-token`. On Unix the file is created **owner-only
  (`0600`)** in a single syscall so the token is never momentarily world-readable.
- **Every endpoint except `/health`** (a data-free liveness probe) requires
  `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. The token is compared in **constant time** to
  avoid leaking a timing signal, and a mismatch returns `401`.
- The MCP `resources/read` channel is **scoped to advertised vault/recents
  files** (it cannot be used to read arbitrary paths off disk) and, like
  the tools below, it reads only Markdown non-dotfiles after resolving
  symlinks.
- Conversation memory under `~/.mdopener/sessions` is **owner-only**: the
  server keeps the directory `0700` and writes each session file `0600`.
- Searches (`search_vault`, `text://vault-search` and the app's `/search`)
  read only the vault files and recents that are Markdown documents and not
  dotfiles, checked after resolving symlinks, so a recent `.env` or a
  `notes.md` link to a key is never searched.
- The tools that read a path straight from disk (`diff_documents`,
  `export_text` / `export_metadata` with `path`, `search_vault` with `vault`
  when the app is unreachable, and the task list of
  `get_user_annotations` for a file that is not the open document) only read Markdown files
  (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd`, `.mdx`) that are not dotfiles. The
  check runs after symlinks are resolved, so a `notes.md` link to `.env` is
  refused with `isError: true`. The read then takes only the file the check
  saw: on Unix a link put in the file's place afterwards is not followed
  (`O_NOFOLLOW`), and a file with another device and inode (its folder
  swapped for a link, say) is refused. The app's `/search` and
  `/annotations` read the same way. The tools that ask the app to open a path
  (`open_file`, `present_document`, `request_review` with `path`) make the
  same check, since the app would then show the file and
  `get_current_content` would return it; the app's `/open`, `/present` and
  `/review` endpoints refuse such a path too (HTTP 400, and the reason
  reaches the agent). `edit_canvas` likewise re-checks `.canvas`
  after resolving symlinks, and saves by renaming a new temp file over the
  canvas (keeping its permissions), so a canvas swapped for a symlink after
  the check is replaced, never written through.
- `export` with `output_path` writes that file without a dialog, and replaces
  an existing file of that name only with `overwrite: true`. It only accepts a non-dotfile path with the
  format's own extension (`.html`/`.htm`, `.docx`, `.epub`) in an existing
  directory, so it cannot overwrite Markdown or other file types. The app's
  `/export` endpoint applies the same rule to `outputPath` (which must also be
  absolute) and refuses anything else with HTTP 400, whoever calls it. It
  replaces a file already at `outputPath` only when the request says
  `"overwrite": true`; without the flag (a caller written before it existed)
  the file is refused, not replaced.
- Every disk read (those tools, `edit_canvas`, `file://` resources, the
  recent-documents resource and the local grep fallback) opens regular files
  only, so a FIFO or device named `x.md` is refused (or skipped) instead of
  blocking the server. Each also refuses (or, for search and the
  recent-documents resource, skips) a file larger than 16 MiB, the most the
  app accepts in one request, instead of reading it whole into memory and
  into the reply. Session files are read up to 16 MiB too. The app reads
  the same way when the human opens a document or searches from the
  window: regular files only, opened without blocking, at most 16 MiB (the
  document `/content` returns was read that way).
- An answer from the app's IPC server (or from Ollama) is read up to 64 MiB,
  headers included; a longer one is refused ("more than 64 MiB") instead of
  being read into memory for as long as the peer keeps sending.
- The token and port files are **removed on clean app exit**, so a stale process
  can't authenticate against a new session.

---

## Dev / build-from-source

```bash
# Full install (macOS: builds and installs the app, sidecars, and CLI;
# elsewhere: CLI + MCP only, get the app from Releases):
bash <(curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/main/scripts/install.sh)

# Or from a checkout:
bash scripts/install.sh

# CLI + MCP only (no Tauri app build):
SKIP_APP_BUILD=1 bash scripts/install.sh
```

The install script requires **Rust** (rustup), **Bun** and **git**. It is a
bash script for macOS and Linux. On macOS the full install also needs Xcode
(see the script header). On Linux it builds and installs only `mdopen` and
`mdopener-mcp` (a C toolchain such as `build-essential` is enough) and says so;
install the app itself from a `.deb`, `.rpm` or `.AppImage` release.

In a dev build the MCP binary lives at:

```
src-tauri/target/release/mdopener-mcp
```

Register it with Claude Code:

```bash
claude mcp add --scope user ashlr-md \
  "$(pwd)/src-tauri/target/release/mdopener-mcp"
```

---

## Troubleshooting

**"binary not found" after connecting**
The MCP binary must exist before the agent can launch it. Either:
- Install the full app from a release DMG or `scripts/install.sh`, or
- Run `cargo build --release --manifest-path src-tauri/Cargo.toml -p mdopener-mcp`
  from the repo root and register the `src-tauri/target/release/mdopener-mcp`
  path manually.

**Tools return "Ashlr MD does not appear to be running"**
The app must be open for everything except `open_file`. Launch Ashlr MD (or call
`open_file`, which cold-starts it), then retry. A tool that was given a `path`
(`request_review`, `present_document`, `edit_document`, `stream_edit`,
`stream_edit_apply`) names the call to make with that exact path, for example
`Call open_file with {"path":"/abs/plan.md"}, which starts it with this
document, then call this tool again.` `stream_edit_apply` says instead to call
`stream_edit` again for a fresh preview before applying: the `editId` of a
preview from before the app started no longer exists, and the document may
have changed since. The message also says that an
app that is not installed comes from
[the releases page](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases).

**Tools return "Ashlr MD answered on the port in ~/.mdopener/ipc-port but refused the token"**
The app answered HTTP 401: `~/.mdopener/ipc-token` is stale, or the port
belongs to another Ashlr MD instance. Every app tool returns this one message
(it used to be the bare "IPC auth failed: token mismatch or missing
~/.mdopener/ipc-token"), and it says the next step: ask the user to quit every
Ashlr MD window fully and start the app again, which writes a new
`~/.mdopener/ipc-port` and `~/.mdopener/ipc-token`, then retry the call.
`open_file` returns it too, without trying the `mdopener://` URL. A
`request_review` that hits it while waiting adds that restarting ends the
review, so request a new one. `get_user_annotations` does not fail on it: it
reads the tasks from disk and says so with `appAuthFailed: true`, and
`search_vault` with `vault` searches that folder on disk, with a `note`
saying why and how to fix it; without `vault`, its error adds "To search
without the app, pass `vault`", as it does for an app that is not running.

**Claude Code shows "ashlr-md: failed to start"**
Run `claude mcp list` to see the registered path, then verify the binary exists
at that path and is executable (`chmod +x`). Running
`<path> --version` prints `mdopener-mcp <version>` and exits, so it is a quick
check that the path is right (`--help` prints usage). Any other argument is
ignored, so an old client config that passes one still starts the server, but
it is named on stderr (`ignoring unknown argument ...`); look there in the
client's MCP log for a typo such as `--verison`. That holds for an argument
that is not valid UTF-8 too (it used to stop the server with a panic). Run from a terminal, it says
on stderr that it is waiting for JSON-RPC on stdin; stdout carries only
protocol messages.

**Cursor MCP panel shows the server as offline**
Restart Cursor. If the issue persists, open `~/.cursor/mcp.json` and confirm the
`command` path points to the binary.

**Auto-open hook didn't install**
If `~/.claude/settings.json` has a malformed `hooks` / `hooks.PostToolUse` shape,
the installer bails rather than overwrite it; fix the JSON manually and retry.

**`mdopen` command not found after installing**
On macOS/Linux, make sure `/usr/local/bin` (or `~/.local/bin`) is on your `$PATH`:
```bash
echo $PATH          # check
mdopen --help       # verify
```
On Windows, add the folder holding `mdopen.exe` (`%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin`
after **Install mdopen**, or the app's install folder) to your user `PATH`, then
restart your terminal. The in-app installer does not change `PATH`.


## Source: docs/INSTALL.md

Canonical documentation: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/INSTALL.md

# Installing Ashlr MD

Ashlr MD is available for macOS (Apple Silicon), Windows (x64) and Linux (x86_64)
from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/latest).
There are no Homebrew, winget or AUR packages yet.

---

## macOS

### DMG

1. Go to [github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/latest](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/latest).
2. Download `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_aarch64.dmg` (Apple Silicon, M1 or later). The
   current release has no Intel build; on an Intel Mac, build from source (see
   the README).
3. Open the DMG, drag **Ashlr MD.app** to `/Applications`.
4. On first launch, right-click the app and choose **Open** to bypass Gatekeeper
   (required for unsigned/unnotarized builds; see note below).

> **Note on Gatekeeper:** Current releases are not notarized with an Apple
> Developer ID, so macOS shows a warning. Right-click → Open bypasses this one
> time. Once you have opened it this way, future launches work normally.

### Set Ashlr MD as the default Markdown app (macOS)

1. Right-click any `.md` file in Finder → **Get Info**.
2. Under **Open with**, select **Ashlr MD**.
3. Click **Change All…** to apply to all `.md` files.

---

## Windows

### Option A: NSIS Installer (recommended)

1. Go to [github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/latest](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/latest).
2. Download `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe`.
3. Run the installer. It installs for the current user to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ashlr MD\`
   by default.
4. If Windows Defender SmartScreen appears, click **More info → Run anyway**.
   (This warning appears for unsigned installers. It will disappear once the
   app is code-signed with an EV/OV certificate.)

> **Silent install** (for IT/automation):
> ```bat
> Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe /S
> ```

The installer puts the `mdopen` CLI (`mdopen.exe`) and the `mdopener-mcp` MCP
server (`mdopener-mcp.exe`) next to the app in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ashlr MD\`.
Neither is on your `PATH` after install. Use **Preferences → Command-line tool
→ Install mdopen**, which copies `mdopen.exe` to `%USERPROFILE%\.local\bin\`
(add that folder to your user `PATH`), or call it by its full path:
`& "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\Ashlr MD\mdopen.exe" notes.md` in PowerShell.

### Option B: MSI Package

Download `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64_en-US.msi` from the same release page.
Double-click to install, or deploy silently via Group Policy / MDM.

### Set Ashlr MD as the default Markdown app (Windows)

The NSIS installer registers `.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd`, and `.mdx`
file associations automatically. To change the default:

1. Right-click a `.md` file → **Open with → Choose another app**.
2. Select **Ashlr MD** → tick **Always use this app** → OK.

---

## Linux

### Option A: Debian / Ubuntu (.deb)

```bash
# Download the .deb from the latest release
curl -L \
  "https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/latest/download/Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb" \
  -o ashlr-md.deb

# Install
sudo dpkg -i ashlr-md.deb

# Fix any missing dependencies
sudo apt-get install -f
```

The `.deb` installs:
- App binary at `/usr/bin/md-opener`
- `.desktop` entry at `/usr/share/applications/Ashlr MD.desktop`
- The `mdopen` CLI and the `mdopener-mcp` MCP server in `/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/`
- Icons under `/usr/share/icons/hicolor/`

`mdopen` is not on your `PATH` after install. Use **Preferences → Command-line
tool → Install mdopen**, or call it by its full path:
`"/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopen" notes.md`.

After install, `.md` files will appear in **Open With → Ashlr MD** in Nautilus
and other XDG-compliant file managers.

### Fedora / RHEL (.rpm)

Download `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x86_64.rpm` from the latest release and install it with
`sudo dnf install ./Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x86_64.rpm`.

### Option B: AppImage (portable, any distro)

```bash
# Download the AppImage
curl -L \
  "https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/latest/download/Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.AppImage" \
  -o AshlrMD.AppImage

# Make executable and run
chmod +x AshlrMD.AppImage
./AshlrMD.AppImage
```

The first time it runs, the AppImage registers the `mdopener://` scheme for
your user (a hidden `md-opener-handler.desktop` entry under
`~/.local/share/applications/` that points at the AppImage), so `mdopen` and
agent deep links reach it. If you move the AppImage, run it once from its new
place to update that entry. It does not add a launcher, icons or an **Open
With** entry for `.md` files; for that, use a desktop integration tool such
as [appimaged](https://github.com/probonopd/go-appimage) or AppImageLauncher.

> The AppImage bundles all dependencies and runs on any x86_64 Linux distro
> with glibc ≥ 2.35 (Ubuntu 22.04+, Fedora 36+, etc.).

### Set Ashlr MD as the default Markdown app (Linux)

With the `.deb` or `.rpm` installed, use **Preferences → Default Markdown app →
Make Default**, or run `xdg-mime` yourself. The desktop entry is named after
the product, with a space, so quote it:

```bash
# Register the MIME type association
xdg-mime default "Ashlr MD.desktop" text/markdown
xdg-mime default "Ashlr MD.desktop" text/x-markdown

# Verify
xdg-mime query default text/markdown
# → Ashlr MD.desktop
```

### Linux troubleshooting

Checked against the v0.4.0 `.deb` and AppImage on Debian 13 (x86_64).

**`dpkg -i` stops with unmet dependencies.** The `.deb` depends on
`libwebkit2gtk-4.1-0` and `libgtk-3-0`. Install it with apt instead, which pulls
those in for you:

```bash
sudo apt-get install ./Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb
```

**Connecting an agent when you use the AppImage.** `mdopener-mcp` lives inside
the AppImage, which is mounted at a different temporary path on every run, so
there is no `/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp` to point Claude Code, Codex or
Cursor at. Either install the `.deb` or `.rpm`, or extract the AppImage once and
use the extracted copy:

```bash
./Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.AppImage --appimage-extract
# Stable path to the MCP server:
"$PWD/squashfs-root/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/mdopener-mcp"
```

Extract again after you update the AppImage, so the agent runs the new version.

**`Cannot mount AppImage, please check your FUSE setup.`** The AppImage uses
the static type 2 runtime, so it does not need `libfuse2` (it ran on Debian 13
with only libfuse3 installed). Where FUSE is not available at all, for example
in a container without `/dev/fuse`, run it without mounting:

```bash
./Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.AppImage --appimage-extract-and-run
```

**`mdopen: command not found`.** Neither package puts `mdopen` on your `PATH`;
see the note under Option A above.

---

## Auto-Updates

Ashlr MD checks for updates a few seconds after each launch (all platforms)
using the Tauri updater. When a new version is available, it asks whether to
install it. Click **Install** to download and install; the app relaunches into
the new version. **Later** dismisses the prompt until the next launch.

There is no menu command to check by hand: quit and reopen the app to check
again. A failed check (offline, for example) is silent.

---

## Uninstalling

| Platform | Method |
|---|---|
| macOS DMG | Drag `Ashlr MD.app` from `/Applications` to Trash |
| Windows | Settings → Apps → Ashlr MD → Uninstall |
| Linux .deb | `sudo apt remove ashlr-md` |
| Linux .rpm | `sudo dnf remove ashlr-md` |
| Linux AppImage | Delete the `.AppImage` file, and `~/.local/share/applications/md-opener-handler.desktop` (the `mdopener://` handler it registered) |

Preferences and app data are stored at:
- **macOS:** `~/Library/Application Support/app.mdopener.desktop`
- **Windows:** `%APPDATA%\app.mdopener.desktop`
- **Linux:** `~/.config/app.mdopener.desktop`

On every platform the app and its agent tools also keep `~/.mdopener/`
(`%USERPROFILE%\.mdopener\` on Windows): the IPC port and token files and
`sessions/`, the conversation memory agents save. A copy made with **Install
mdopen** stays where it was copied too.

These are not removed by a standard uninstall; delete them manually if you
want a clean slate.


## Source: docs/OBSIDIAN.md

Canonical documentation: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/OBSIDIAN.md

# Obsidian compatibility

Ashlr MD reads [Obsidian](https://obsidian.md) vaults and notes natively. Point
it at a `.md` file in your vault and your wikilinks, embeds, highlights,
comments, math, and `.canvas` files all render the way they do in Obsidian's
Reading View, with no plugins and no export step.

It is a **respectful guest** in your vault: Ashlr MD resolves links vault-wide,
opens linked notes in tabs, and can hand a note back to Obsidian in one click,
but it **never writes into your `.obsidian/` config folder** (see
[Vault setup](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/OBSIDIAN.md#vault-setup)).

> This is a *compatibility* layer, not a re-implementation of Obsidian. Anything
> not listed under [What's not supported yet](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/OBSIDIAN.md#whats-not-supported-yet) below
> should behave the way you expect; if it doesn't, that's a bug.

---

## Vault setup

A "vault" is just a folder Obsidian manages. Obsidian marks the vault root with a
`.obsidian/` config directory. Ashlr MD uses that same marker to find your vault
so it can resolve `[[wikilinks]]` across the whole tree (not just the current
folder).

**How the vault root is found**, in order of precedence:

1. **Settings override.** If you set a vault folder in **Settings → Vault**, that
   path is always used as the vault root.
2. **Auto-detection.** Otherwise, Ashlr MD walks up from the open document's
   folder looking for the nearest ancestor that contains a `.obsidian/` folder,
   and uses that directory as the vault root.
3. **Fallback.** If neither is found (e.g. a loose `.md` file outside any vault),
   link resolution falls back to the document's own directory.

Setting the override in **Settings → Vault** is useful when you keep notes
outside a formal Obsidian vault, or when you want resolution scoped to a specific
folder regardless of where the open file lives.

### Ashlr MD never writes to `.obsidian/`

Saving a document is **refused** if the target path lands inside an `.obsidian/`
config folder. The guard checks the path textually *and* resolves symlinks, so a
symlinked config dir can't slip a write past it. Your Obsidian settings, themes,
and plugin configuration are never touched by Ashlr MD.

---

## Wikilinks

Type-through `[[...]]` internal links render as clickable links. Click one to
open the resolved note in a tab; a link carrying a `#heading` anchor also scrolls
to that heading once the note loads. Links that don't resolve are styled as
**broken** and disabled, with the unresolved target shown on hover.

### Supported grammar

| Syntax | What it does |
|---|---|
| `[[note]]` | Link to `note`; the link text is `note`. |
| `[[note\|alias]]` | Link to `note`, displayed as `alias`. |
| `[[note#heading]]` | Link to `note` and scroll to the `heading` section. Default text is `note › heading`. |
| `[[note#^block]]` | Link to `note` (the `^block` anchor is preserved; there's no rendered jump target for block refs yet, so it opens the note without scrolling). |
| `[[#heading]]` | The bare-target form follows the same resolution rules; an empty file part doesn't resolve to a note. |

Aliases and a single `#anchor` can be combined, e.g.
`[[note#heading|see the setup]]`.

### How a link resolves (vault-wide, closest match)

Resolution mirrors Obsidian. The `#heading` / `#^block` fragment is stripped
first; only the file part is resolved. Then, in order:

1. **Exact relative path** from the current note's folder
   (e.g. `[[subfolder/note]]`).
2. **Vault-relative path** from the vault root (Obsidian's `[[folder/note]]`
   from the root).
3. **Relative path + a Markdown extension** appended (current folder, then vault
   root). Recognized extensions: `.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd`, `.mdx`.
4. **Vault-wide name match.** Every Markdown file in the vault whose *name*
   matches (case-insensitively, by file stem) is collected, then the **closest**
   one is chosen: a path that ends with the full link target wins first, then the
   file sharing the longest folder path with the current note (proximity), then
   the shortest path. Ties are broken deterministically, so the same link always
   resolves to the same file.

A target that carries an explicit extension (e.g. an image embed
`![[diagram.png]]`) is matched by **full file name** instead of by Markdown
stem. The vault scan skips hidden folders (including `.obsidian/`),
`node_modules`, and `target`, and is depth- and count-bounded so resolution stays
fast on large vaults.

---

## Embeds & transclusion

Prefix a wikilink with `!` to **embed** the target inline (`![[...]]`). Embeds
render through the same renderer, so nested Markdown, callouts, and math all work
inside an embed. Recursive embeds are capped (depth 3) so an `a → b → a` cycle
can't loop forever.

| Syntax | What it does |
|---|---|
| `![[note]]` | Transclude the **entire** note inline, under a title bar. |
| `![[note#heading]]` | Transclude just that **heading's section**: the heading plus everything under it up to the next same-or-higher-level heading. |
| `![[note#^block]]` | Transclude just the **single block** (paragraph / list item) tagged with that `^block` id; the `^id` marker is stripped from the output. |
| `![[image.png]]` | Embed the image inline. |
| `![[image.png\|300]]` | Embed the image at **300px wide**. |
| `![[image.png\|300x200]]` | Embed the image at **300×200px**. |

Image embeds support `png`, `jpg`/`jpeg`, `gif`, `svg`, `webp`, `bmp`, and
`avif`. Images are read through the Rust core into an inline `data:` URL (so the
webview never needs broad filesystem access) and are capped at 25 MiB per image.
If a partial-embed fragment can't be located, the **full** note is embedded so
the embed still shows something useful.

---

## Highlights, comments & math

| Syntax | Rendering |
|---|---|
| `==highlight==` | Rendered as a highlighted `<mark>`. Empty / whitespace-only delimiters (`== ==`) are left as plain text. |
| `%%comment%%` | **Hidden** in the reading view, matching Obsidian: the delimiters and their content are removed. Inline comments only; comments that span paragraph boundaries are left as-is. |
| `$inline math$` | Inline math via KaTeX. |
| `$$display math$$` | Display (block) math via KaTeX. |

Highlight and comment markers inside code spans / code blocks are treated as
literal text and are never transformed.

---

## Canvas (`.canvas`)

Ashlr MD opens [JSON Canvas](https://jsoncanvas.org) (`.canvas`) files in a
**read-only** viewer. Drag the background to **pan**, scroll to **zoom**, and use
**Fit** (or the `+` / `−` buttons) to frame the whole canvas. The view auto-fits
on open.

**Node types that render:**

| Node | Rendering |
|---|---|
| `text` | The node's Markdown, rendered through the same renderer. |
| `file` | A titled card embedding the linked file's Markdown or, for an image file, the inline image. The title is a button that opens the file in a tab. |
| `link` | A card showing the external URL. Only `http(s):` and `mailto:` URLs are clickable; anything else (e.g. `javascript:`) is shown as inert text. |
| `group` | A labelled rectangle drawn behind its member nodes. |

**Edges** render as connectors with optional labels and arrowheads (Obsidian's
default arrow-at-destination is honored). Node and edge **colors** use Obsidian's
six-color preset palette as well as raw hex values.

Canvas is read-only: node positions and the canvas file are **never written
back**.

---

## Round-trip: Open in Obsidian

Any open note can be handed back to Obsidian with the **Open in Obsidian**
command (in the command palette, `⌘K`). It launches Obsidian on that exact file
via the `obsidian://open?path=…` URI scheme, so you can edit graph-heavy notes,
run plugins, or use any Obsidian feature, then jump back to Ashlr MD for a fast,
beautiful read. (Obsidian must be installed.)

The companion **[Open in Ashlr MD](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/integrations/obsidian/)** Obsidian plugin
closes the loop the other way: a ribbon icon, command, and right-click menu send
the current vault note to Ashlr MD via the `mdopener://` scheme.

---

## What's not supported yet

Ashlr MD aims to *read* a vault faithfully, not to replace Obsidian's editor.
The following are intentionally absent today:

- **Editing or creating canvases.** `.canvas` files are view-only; positions and
  content are never written back.
- **Obsidian community/core plugins** (Dataview, Templater, Tasks, etc.). Ashlr
  MD renders standard Markdown + the syntax documented above; plugin-specific
  query blocks and processors are not evaluated.
- **Block-reference jump targets.** A `[[note#^block]]` link opens the note but
  doesn't scroll to the block (heading anchors *do* scroll). Block *embeds*
  (`![[note#^block]]`) do work.
- **Multi-line / block `%%comments%%`** that span paragraph boundaries; only
  inline comments are hidden.
- **Obsidian-specific frontmatter behaviors** (aliases-as-link-targets, custom
  link-resolution settings, per-vault Markdown extension config). Link resolution
  follows the rules documented above, not your vault's individual settings.

If something in your vault doesn't render the way Obsidian's Reading View shows
it, and it isn't in this list, please
[open an issue](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/issues).


## Source: docs/PHANTOM.md

Canonical documentation: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/PHANTOM.md

# Ashlr MD in Phantom

[Phantom](https://github.com/ashlrai/phantom) uses Ashlr MD as its Markdown viewer.
When Phantom has Markdown to show a human (`phm inbox show <id> --open`,
`phm digest --open`) and Ashlr MD is installed, Phantom hands the file to
Ashlr MD; otherwise it falls back to terminal output.

> **Status on Phantom `master`:** only the inbox/digest viewer seam
> (`src/core/integrations/markdown.ts`, `presentMarkdown`) is merged. It detects
> Ashlr MD with `which mdopen` and runs `mdopen <file>`. The "open any `.md` in
> Ashlr MD" opener for `phantom open` and the web/desktop **Open** action, its
> `"markdownOpener": "editor"` / `PHANTOM_ASHLR_MD=0` opt-outs, and
> `docs/companions/ashlr-md.md` live on Phantom's unmerged
> `feat/ashlr-md-opener` branch, not on `master`.

## Integration contract (stable hooks Phantom relies on)

| Hook | Shape | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| URL scheme | `mdopener://open?path=<url-encoded absolute path>[&mode=edit]` | Defined in `src-tauri/tauri.conf.json` (`deep-link.desktop.schemes`). |
| CLI | `mdopen <file.md>` | Phantom treats `mdopen` on `PATH` as "installed". Exit status below. |
| MCP | `mdopener-mcp` → `open_file { path, mode? }` | For agents running under Phantom that want a human to review a document. See [AGENTS.md](https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/AGENTS.md). |

### `mdopen` exit status

`mdopen` opens only Markdown documents (`.md`, `.markdown`, `.mdown`, `.mkd`,
`.mdx`) that are not dotfiles, checked after symlinks are resolved; anything
else exits `1` before the app is contacted. When Ashlr MD is running, `mdopen`
hands it the file over its loopback IPC channel. Otherwise it hands the
`mdopener://` URL to the OS launcher (`open` on macOS,
`xdg-open` then `gio open` on Linux, `rundll32 url.dll,FileProtocolHandler` on Windows) and waits at
most 10 seconds for it. The launcher never gets `mdopen`'s stdin or stdout.

| Exit | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `0` | The running app accepted the file, or the launcher accepted the URL. If the launcher is still running after 10 s, `mdopen` prints `... the open is not confirmed` on stderr and still exits `0`. |
| `1` | Bad usage, a missing or unresolvable path, a file that is not a Markdown document or is a dotfile, the running app refused the file (its reason is on stderr, and the URL scheme is not tried), the running app was reached but failed: it answered with a server error, the connection broke, or it did not answer within 6 s (the URL scheme is not tried, since the app may still open the file, and a `mdopen -` temp file is kept), the launcher failed (no handler for `mdopener://`, no display), or no launcher exists. stderr says which. |

`mdopen --hook` (the Claude Code `PostToolUse` hook) exits `0` and prints
nothing, waiting at most 5 seconds for the launcher. It opens only the Markdown
file a `PostToolUse` payload from `Write`, `Edit` or `MultiEdit` names; a
payload naming another `hook_event_name` or `tool_name`, or whose
`tool_response` reports the tool failed, opens nothing. Run by hand with a
terminal on stdin (nothing piped in), it prints a hint on stderr and exits `0`
at once instead of waiting for a payload. The one exception is a hook command
with another argument (`mdopen --hook notes.md`): the payload comes on stdin,
so that is a usage error, exit `1` with the argument named on stderr.

A caller that wants to know whether the viewer opened must wait for `mdopen` to
exit and check for `0`. Spawning it detached and ignoring the status reports
success on a headless machine, where `mdopen` exits `1`.

### `mdopener-mcp`

Speaks MCP over stdio. `initialize` echoes `2024-11-05`, `2025-03-26` and
`2025-06-18`, and answers any other requested version with `2025-06-18`.
`open_file` accepts only a Markdown document that is not a dotfile and that
exists (checked after symlinks are resolved); any other path is refused with
`isError: true` before the app or the URL scheme is reached, and a running app
that refuses the file is not retried through the URL scheme.
When the app is not running, `open_file` falls back to the URL scheme through
the same launchers as `mdopen` (bounded at 10 seconds). When nothing could
open it, for example on a headless Linux box, the call returns a tool result
with `isError: true` whose text names the launcher outcome. `mode` must be
`read` or `edit`.

Tool failures (app not reachable, a file that cannot be read or written, an
operation the app rejects) come back as a successful `tools/call` result with
`isError: true` and the reason as text, per the MCP spec, so the agent can
read it and act. JSON-RPC errors are kept for protocol problems: an unknown
tool or method, or invalid arguments (`-32602`).

## Detection paths

`mdopen` on `PATH`; macOS `/Applications/Ashlr MD.app` or `~/Applications/Ashlr MD.app`;
Windows `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Ashlr MD\Ashlr MD.exe`; Linux `/usr/bin/md-opener`
(or `/usr/bin/ashlr-md`) or an `Ashlr MD.desktop` entry.

On a Linux `.deb` install the sidecars (`mdopen`, `mdopener-mcp`) land in
`/usr/lib/Ashlr MD/`, which is not on `PATH`. `mdopen` is on `PATH` only after
**Install mdopen** in Settings (`/usr/local/bin` or `~/.local/bin`) or the
source installer. A detector that only runs `which mdopen` (Phantom `master`)
misses a fresh `.deb` install.

Changing the product name, bundle path, or the `mdopener` scheme is a breaking
change for Phantom; update Phantom's Markdown integration alongside it.

## Opting out (Phantom side)

On the `feat/ashlr-md-opener` branch: `"markdownOpener": "editor"` in Phantom's
config, or `PHANTOM_ASHLR_MD=0`. On `master`, simply omit `--open`.

## Running under `phantom exec` (Phantom Secrets)

`phantom exec -- <cmd>` does three things:
- It starts `<cmd>` with `phm_` session placeholders instead of real provider keys.
- It points provider base URLs such as `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` at a local Phantom proxy: `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/<route>/_phantom/<token>/`.
- On the way out, the proxy swaps each placeholder for the real key.

What Ashlr MD reads, at call time:

| Setting | Used by | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` | AI sidebar (Anthropic) | `https://` to any host, or plain `http://` only to `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`. Anything else is refused before the key is attached. The Phantom proxy URL is loopback http, so it is accepted. |
| `ASHLR_MD_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FROM_ENV` | AI sidebar (Anthropic) | Exactly `1` turns on reading the key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` instead of Settings. Unset, or any other value, means Settings only (the default). |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | AI sidebar and semantic search (Ollama) | Taken as given: `host`, `host:port`, `:port` or a full URL. |
| `OLLAMA_HOST` | MCP sidecar (`mdopener-mcp`) embeddings | Since #138: `https://` to any host, or plain `http://` only to `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]`. `:port`, `0.0.0.0` and `[::]` map to loopback, and redirects are refused. |

Things to know:
- **The Anthropic key comes from Settings by default.** The app sends the key saved in Settings, which is stored in the OS keychain, and ignores `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`. To use the `phm_` placeholder from `phantom exec` instead, opt in with `ASHLR_MD_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FROM_ENV=1` (see below).
- **Shell-launched only.** An app launched from the Dock or Start menu does not see variables from your shell or from `phantom exec`. Start its executable from that shell instead: for example `phantom exec -- /usr/bin/md-opener` on a Linux `.deb` install, or the executable inside `Ashlr MD.app/Contents/MacOS/` on macOS. `open -a` hands the launch to the OS and may not pass the variables. These launch forms have not been tested here.
- **The sidecar has no key.** `mdopener-mcp` sends no Anthropic requests and attaches no key to Ollama requests. An agent that runs it under `phantom exec` needs no placeholder for it.
- **No `phm:` references.** Ashlr MD never resolves a `phm:` reference. Do not use `phantom reveal` to copy a key into Settings or into the environment.

### Using `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the environment (opt-in)

```sh
ASHLR_MD_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FROM_ENV=1 phantom exec -- /usr/bin/md-opener
```

With `ASHLR_MD_ANTHROPIC_KEY_FROM_ENV=1`, the AI sidebar takes the Anthropic key from `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` at request time:
- **Only the environment key is used.** The key saved in Settings is not sent, and there is no fallback to it. Settings shows a note that the environment key is in use.
- **The value stays in the Rust process.** It is never sent to the webview, written to Settings or the keychain, logged, or included in an error message. The webview only learns whether the opt-in is on, whether the key is usable, and whether it is a `phm_` placeholder.
- **A `phm_` placeholder needs the session proxy.** `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` must be set and pass the usual rules. It must point at `127.0.0.1` or `[::1]` with a port, and that port must be `PHANTOM_PROXY_PORT` when it is set. Without that, the placeholder would go to the real provider, so the request is refused.
- **A real key** in `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` is accepted with any `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` that passes the usual rules.
- **Refused before any request:** an unset or blank key, a `phm:` reference (Ashlr MD does not resolve references), or a value with spaces or control characters. The reason is shown, but the value never is.
- **Request errors leave out the URL**, so the per-session proxy token in the path is not shown.

The rules and the webview side are covered by tests: `src-tauri/src/base_urls.rs` and `src/ai/anthropicEnvKey.test.ts`. It has not been tested against a live `phantom exec` session.

### LiteLLM

If a LiteLLM proxy sits in front of Anthropic or Ollama, use LiteLLM 1.83.0 or newer, never 1.82.7 or 1.82.8.

- **Why 1.83.0:** `litellm` 1.82.7 and 1.82.8 on PyPI were compromised releases that carried credential-stealing code (GHSA-5mg7-485q-xm76, March 2026). 1.83.0, published to PyPI on 2026-03-31, was the first clean release, built by LiteLLM's rebuilt release pipeline ([LiteLLM security update](https://docs.litellm.ai/blog/security-update-march-2026)).
- **Use a current release, not just 1.83.0.** Later advisories were fixed in later releases (for example GHSA-3cv6-jpf6-8222). On 2026-10-19 the current PyPI release was 1.106.0. Check LiteLLM's security advisories before you pick or upgrade a version.
- **Install it verifiably.** Use a hash-pinned install (`pip install --require-hashes -r requirements.txt`) or the official `ghcr.io/berriai/litellm` image, checked with `cosign verify` as LiteLLM's README shows. Run it in a container that does not mount your home directory or dotfiles.
- Keep the provider keys on the LiteLLM side. Give the agent only the proxy URL and, if the proxy needs one, a proxy key that is separate from the provider keys.

For Ashlr MD, `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` points at the gateway root, and the app appends `/v1/messages`, so the gateway must serve the Anthropic Messages API there. Use `https://`, or `http://127.0.0.1:<port>` for a proxy on the same machine. Only the URL handling is covered by tests. The app has not been tested against a live LiteLLM or Phantom proxy.


## Source: docs/PQ-READINESS.md

Canonical documentation: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/PQ-READINESS.md

# Post-quantum readiness

Status as of 2026-10-17. This note records what ashlr-md does with cryptography today and what a post-quantum migration would touch. It makes no claim that ashlr-md is quantum-safe or quantum-resistant, and it adds no new cryptography.

## Background (verified against NIST pages)
- NIST published FIPS 203 (ML-KEM), FIPS 204 (ML-DSA) and FIPS 205 (SLH-DSA) on August 13, 2024. Source: https://csrc.nist.gov/Projects/Post-Quantum-Cryptography/Post-Quantum-Cryptography-Standardization
- Shor's algorithm would break RSA and elliptic-curve schemes (RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, X25519, Ed25519) on a large enough quantum computer. Grover's algorithm gives a quadratic speedup on brute-force search, so symmetric keys are usually sized at 256 bits.
- Harvest-now-decrypt-later applies to confidentiality: ciphertext captured today, protected only by classical key exchange, could be read later. Signatures are different: they matter when they are verified, so the risk is forgery after a capable quantum computer exists.

## What ashlr-md uses today
- No cryptographic primitives are implemented in the application source (TypeScript front end, Rust `src-tauri`, `mdopener-mcp`). The inventory scan finds no RSA, ECDSA, ECDH, Ed25519 or X25519 use.
- Dependencies that bring crypto with them, listed from `src-tauri/Cargo.toml` and not audited here: `keyring` (OS credential store), `reqwest` (HTTP client) and `tauri-plugin-updater`. Which algorithms they use is decided by those crates and the platform, and this note does not claim anything about them. The scan cannot see inside dependencies.
- The loopback IPC token is random bytes (see the comment in `src-tauri/Cargo.toml`); it is a shared secret, not a public-key scheme.

## The check
`scripts/check-crypto.mjs` scans source files (not tests, docs or vendored directories) for classical asymmetric primitives: RSA, ECDSA/ECDH, Ed25519/X25519 and Diffie-Hellman key generation. It prints an inventory and exits 1 when a file that is not in its `ALLOW` list uses one, so a new classical-only use needs a deliberate decision with a written reason. It does not judge hashes, HMAC or symmetric ciphers, and it is a regex scan, not a parser: it can miss indirect use through a dependency. Run it with `node scripts/check-crypto.mjs`; its tests run with `node --test scripts/check-crypto.test.mjs`.

## Library note
No post-quantum library is used here, because there is no concrete use that needs one. If one is added later, `@noble/post-quantum` 0.7.1 (MIT) offers ML-KEM, ML-DSA and SLH-DSA in TypeScript, but its README states it is not independently audited and not constant-time, so it should not be used for secret-key signing on shared hardware. RustCrypto `ml-kem` and `ml-dsa` carry the same "never independently audited" statement. Any adoption should say so in its docs. Source notes: Phantom's quantum research, /workspace/phantom-work/quantum-research.md.

## If a migration is needed
Watch the dependencies above. The update channel is the place a classical signature would matter most; check the `tauri-plugin-updater` documentation for its signature scheme before making any claim, and track upstream support for post-quantum signatures.


## Source: docs/RELEASING.md

Canonical documentation: https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/blob/main/docs/RELEASING.md

# Releasing Ashlr MD

Complete runbook for cutting a release, managing artifacts, and updating
downstream distribution channels (Homebrew, winget, AUR).

---

## 1. Pre-release Checklist

Before tagging, complete every item:

- [ ] All CI checks passing on `main`.
- [ ] Update `version` in **`src-tauri/tauri.conf.json`** (e.g. `"0.2.0"`).
- [ ] Update `version` in **`src-tauri/Cargo.toml`** `[package]` section to match.
- [ ] Update `version` in **`package.json`** to match.
- [ ] Update **`CHANGELOG.md`**: add a section headed `## [X.Y.Z]`, an em dash and the
  date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), like the earlier releases' headings.
- [ ] Run `./scripts/generate-icons.sh` if `src-tauri/icons/icon.svg` changed.
- [ ] Commit all changes:
  ```bash
  git add src-tauri/tauri.conf.json src-tauri/Cargo.toml package.json CHANGELOG.md
  git commit -m "chore: release vX.Y.Z"
  ```

---

## 2. Cutting the Tag

```bash
git tag vX.Y.Z
git push origin vX.Y.Z
```

This triggers `.github/workflows/release.yml`, which fans out across the full
build matrix and **uploads each platform's bundles as workflow artifacts**.

> **The workflow does NOT create the GitHub Release.** The org disables
> `GITHUB_TOKEN` write access, so `release.yml` is build-only: it never calls
> the Release API and never publishes `latest.json`. A maintainer assembles and
> publishes the Release manually from the uploaded artifacts (see §4). Until
> that manual step is done, **no release exists and the updater sees nothing.**

> **Pre-release tags:** any tag containing a hyphen (`v0.2.0-beta.1`) sets
> `prerelease: true` automatically. Use this for testing the pipeline without
> shipping to stable update channels.

---

## 3. What the Workflow Produces

The Tauri bundler names each file after `productName` (`Ashlr MD`), space
included, and the workflow uploads them under those names. The release
publishes them under the names in the last column, which the install guide,
the Homebrew cask, the winget manifest and the AUR PKGBUILD download (see §4,
step 4).

| Platform | Runner | Bundler output | Publish as |
|---|---|---|---|
| macOS arm64 | `macos-14` | `Ashlr MD_X.Y.Z_aarch64.dmg` | `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_aarch64.dmg` |
| macOS x86_64 | `macos-13` | `Ashlr MD_X.Y.Z_x64.dmg` | `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64.dmg` |
| Linux x86_64 | `ubuntu-22.04` | `Ashlr MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb` | `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb` |
| Linux x86_64 | `ubuntu-22.04` | `Ashlr MD-X.Y.Z-1.x86_64.rpm` | `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x86_64.rpm` |
| Linux x86_64 | `ubuntu-22.04` | `Ashlr MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.AppImage` | `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.AppImage` |
| Windows x86_64 | `windows-latest` | `Ashlr MD_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe` (NSIS) | `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe` |
| Windows x86_64 | `windows-latest` | `Ashlr MD_X.Y.Z_x64_en-US.msi` | `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64_en-US.msi` |

Each bundle comes with its updater `.sig` file where the updater signs it.

Each leg uploads a platform-specific entry to the Tauri updater manifest.
After all four legs complete, `latest.json` in the release contains aggregated
entries for every platform; this is what `tauri-plugin-updater` polls.

### Sidecar binaries per platform

| Binary | macOS | Linux | Windows |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mdopen` | yes | yes | yes (`.exe`) |
| `mdopener-mcp` | yes | yes | yes (`.exe`) |
| `mdopener-afm` (Swift) | yes | no | no |
| `mdopener-setdefault` (Swift) | yes | no | no |

> **macOS AFM sidecar risk:** `mdopener-afm` requires Xcode 26 / Swift 6.2+
> (macOS 26 SDK). The workflow selects the latest available Xcode via
> `maxim-lobanov/setup-xcode@v1`. Until GitHub-hosted runners carry Xcode 26,
> this sidecar may build against an older SDK or fail. See the comment block
> in `.github/workflows/release.yml` (the "Select latest Xcode" step) for
> mitigation steps. All other bundle artifacts are unaffected.

---

## 4. Assembling & Publishing the GitHub Release

Because `release.yml` only uploads artifacts (see §2), you assemble the Release
yourself with your own credentials:

1. Open the completed workflow run at **github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/actions**
   and **download every leg's uploaded artifacts** (the `.dmg`/`.deb`/
   `.AppImage`/`.exe`/`.msi` bundles, their `.sig` files, and each leg's updater
   manifest fragment).
2. **Assemble `latest.json`** by merging the per-platform updater entries from
   every leg into one manifest (`version`, `pub_date`, and a `platforms` map of
   `{ signature, url }` per target). The `url` of each entry must point at the
   renamed asset you upload in step 5.
3. Create a new Release at **github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/new** for the
   `vX.Y.Z` tag (mark it pre-release for hyphenated tags). Paste the matching
   `CHANGELOG.md` section as the notes.
4. **Rename each bundle to its "Publish as" name in §3** (the space in
   `Ashlr MD` becomes `_`, and the `.rpm` becomes `Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x86_64.rpm`),
   and each `.sig` to match. Uploaded as built, GitHub turns the space into a
   `.` (`Ashlr.MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb`), and every download link in the docs and
   packaging templates 404s.
5. Attach all renamed bundles **and** the assembled `latest.json` as release
   assets, then **Publish**.

Publishing makes `latest.json` live at the updater endpoint; existing installs
prompt to update on next launch. (If you later automate this, a PAT with
`contents:write` in the workflow would let `tauri-action` create the Release
directly and this manual step goes away.)

---

## 5. Post-release: Update the Homebrew Cask

The canonical cask template lives at `packaging/homebrew/ashlr-md.rb`.
The tap repo is **github.com/ashlrai/homebrew-ashlr-md**; create it if it
doesn't exist yet; place the cask at `Casks/ashlr-md.rb` in that repo.

```bash
# 1. Download the new DMG and compute its SHA-256
curl -L \
  "https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_aarch64.dmg" \
  -o Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_aarch64.dmg
shasum -a 256 Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_aarch64.dmg

# 2. Clone the tap repo and update the cask
git clone https://github.com/ashlrai/homebrew-ashlr-md.git
cd homebrew-ashlr-md

# Edit Casks/ashlr-md.rb:
#   version "X.Y.Z"
#   sha256  "<output of shasum above>"

# 3. Commit and push
git add Casks/ashlr-md.rb
git commit -m "Cask update: ashlr-md X.Y.Z"
git push
```

Users install / upgrade with:
```bash
brew tap ashlrai/ashlr-md
brew install --cask ashlr-md
# upgrade:
brew upgrade --cask ashlr-md
```

---

## 6. Post-release: Update the winget Manifest

The manifest templates live at `packaging/winget/`.

```bash
# 1. Download the NSIS installer and compute its SHA-256
curl -L \
  "https://github.com/ashlrai/ashlr-md/releases/download/vX.Y.Z/Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe" \
  -o Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe

# macOS/Linux:
shasum -a 256 Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe
# Windows PowerShell:
# Get-FileHash "Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_x64-setup.exe" -Algorithm SHA256

# 2. Copy the three manifests to a versioned folder
mkdir -p manifests/a/ashlrai/AshlrMD/X.Y.Z
cp packaging/winget/ashlrai.AshlrMD.*.yaml \
   manifests/a/ashlrai/AshlrMD/X.Y.Z/

# 3. Replace <VERSION> and <SHA256_NSIS_EXE> in all three files

# 4. Validate locally (requires winget CLI or winget-create)
winget validate --manifest manifests/a/ashlrai/AshlrMD/X.Y.Z/

# 5. Fork https://github.com/microsoft/winget-pkgs and submit a PR
#    adding the three manifests under manifests/a/ashlrai/AshlrMD/X.Y.Z/
```

---

## 7. Post-release: Update the AUR Package

The PKGBUILD template lives at `packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD`.

```bash
# 1. Compute SHA-256 of the .deb
shasum -a 256 Ashlr_MD_X.Y.Z_amd64.deb

# 2. Update packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD:
#    pkgver=X.Y.Z
#    sha256sums=('<output of shasum above>')

# 3. Clone your AUR repo (first time: create the package at aur.archlinux.org)
git clone ssh://aur@aur.archlinux.org/ashlr-md.git aur-ashlr-md
cp packaging/linux/aur/PKGBUILD aur-ashlr-md/

# 4. Regenerate .SRCINFO (required by AUR)
cd aur-ashlr-md
makepkg --printsrcinfo > .SRCINFO

# 5. Test the build locally
makepkg -si

# 6. Push to AUR
git add PKGBUILD .SRCINFO
git commit -m "Update to X.Y.Z"
git push
```
